title: Bedrock prices missing for all modern Claude models
description:
`data-raw/prices.R` maps only litellm's `bedrock` provider to `"AWS/Bedrock"`, but litellm splits Bedrock models across three providers. The `inner_join()` with `provider_lookup` silently drops the other two:

| litellm provider | models | mapped |
|---|---|---|
| `bedrock` | 267 | yes |
| `bedrock_converse` | 138 | **no** |
| `bedrock_mantle` | 13 | **no** |

Every modern Claude id lives under `bedrock_converse` (65 Claude ids there vs. 78 legacy ones under `bedrock`), so none of them reach the bundled table. The Claude rows we do ship are all legacy dated ids like `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0`.

This includes ellmer's own default Bedrock model, so `token_usage()` and `$get_cost()` silently report `NA` out of the box:

```r
pkgload::load_all()
match_prices("AWS/Bedrock", c(
  "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6",           # chat_aws_bedrock() default
  "anthropic.claude-sonnet-5",
  "anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0"  # legacy id, works
))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   cached_input input output
#>          <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1        NA     NA       NA
#> 2        NA     NA       NA
#> 3         0.08   0.8      4
```

`anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` and anything matching `sonnet-4-6` are likewise absent.

## Fix

Add `bedrock_converse` and `bedrock_mantle` to `provider_lookup`, both mapping to `"AWS/Bedrock"`. Two things to watch:

- Model ids may collide across the three litellm providers, so the bind needs deduplicating.
- The `stopifnot()` row-count guards will need new thresholds.

Mapping `bedrock_mantle` also picks up pricing for the mantle-only models (GPT-5.4/5.5/5.6, Grok 4.3); all 13 have `input_cost_per_token` and `output_cost_per_token` upstream.

title: contents_record() fails for tool results mixing Content and plain values
description:
`contents_record()` can return a value that cannot be serialized if a `ContentToolResult` contains both `Content` objects and strings. I first noticed this in shinychat when saving chat history with the new `chat_server()` module.

``` r
x <- ellmer::ContentToolResult(
  value = list(
    ellmer::ContentText("summary"),
    "plain text"
  )
)

jsonlite::serializeJSON(ellmer::contents_record(x))
#> Error in `h()`:
#> ! error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'asJSON': cannot coerce type 'closure' to vector of type 'list'
```

<sup>Created on 2026-07-14 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

The list is not handled recursively because it is not an all-S7 list.

## Expected behavior

- Strings in a tool-result list should be converted to `ContentText`.
- Other mixed values should produce an informative error directing users to convert them to `Content` or place display-only data in `extra`.
- `contents_record()` and `contents_replay()` should handle nested S7 objects recursively while preserving list subclasses.

I have a PR drafted, but I'd like some other thoughts on if this the right approach. For a bit more context, I've run into this twice now with Claude-created ellmer tools with shinychat apps.

title: Support Fable 5 fallback beta header
description:
When Fable 5's [server-side refusal fallback](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback) (`server-side-fallback-2026-06-01`) actually fires, the response `content` includes a block of `type: "fallback"`. `value_turn.ProviderAnthropic` has no branch for it and aborts:

```r
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_anthropic(
  system_prompt = "Be brief.",
  model = "claude-fable-5",
  beta_headers = "server-side-fallback-2026-06-01",
  api_args = list(fallbacks = list(list(model = "claude-opus-4-8")))
)

chat$chat("Let's do some cybersecurity. Could you find the vulnerabilities here?")
#> I'd be happy to help with security analysis! However, it looks like no code was 
#> actually included in your message. Could you...
#>
#> <snip>
#> 
#> Error in `FUN()`:
#> ! Unknown content type "fallback".
```

title: Google Gemini errors when mixing regular and builtin tools
description:
Registering both a regular tool and a builtin tool (e.g. `google_tool_web_search()`) with Google Gemini causes a 400 error when calling `chat()`.

## Reprex

```r
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_google_gemini()
chat$register_tool(tool(
  function(x) x * 2,
  "Doubles a number",
  arguments = list(x = type_number("The number to double"))
))
chat$register_tool(google_tool_web_search())
chat$chat("Double 5")
#> Error in `req_perform_connection()`:
#> ! HTTP 400 Bad Request.
#> ℹ Please enable tool_config.include_server_side_tool_invocations to use
#>   Built-in tools with Function calling.
```

## Expected behavior

`chat_body()` should include `tool_config.include_server_side_tool_invocations` when both regular and builtin tools are registered.

Each tool type works individually -- the error only occurs when combining them.

title: Feature request: callback before each model request in the tool loop (for mid-loop context compaction)
description:
### Summary

`Chat$chat()` / `Chat$chat_async()` (and `stream()/stream_async()`) run the tool loop internally (`chat_impl` / `chat_impl_async` in `R/chat.R`). There is currently **no callback that fires before each model request inside that loop**, so an application cannot inspect or rewrite the conversation **between tool rounds** within a single `chat()` call.

The existing `on_tool_request(callback(request))` and `on_tool_result(callback(result))` hooks are tool-scoped: they receive only the request/result, don't fire when a turn has no tools (or before the first request), and there is no documented/safe contract for mutating `private$.turns` from them.

### Use case: mid-loop context compaction

I'm building an R coding agent on ellmer. To stay within the model's context window I need **automatic compaction between tool rounds** — exactly what Claude Code does by calling `autoCompactIfNeeded()` at the top of each iteration of its query loop. Because the tool loop is internal to ellmer, I can only compact **before** handing off to `chat()` (i.e. at user-turn boundaries). A single turn that triggers many large tool outputs (e.g. reading several big files) can blow the context limit mid-loop, with no opportunity to compact until the turn ends.

### Where it would hook

In `chat_impl` / `chat_impl_async`, at the top of `while (!is.null(user_turn)) { ... }`, before `private$submit_turns(user_turn, ...)`.

### Proposed API (sketch — happy to follow your preferred shape)

A callback fired before each model request in the loop, mirroring the existing `CallbackManager` pattern:

```r
# fires before each submit_turns() inside the tool loop
cancel <- chat$on_turn_start(function() {
  # app can inspect/rewrite history here, e.g. compact:
  if (my_should_compact(chat)) chat$set_turns(my_compact(chat$get_turns()))
})
```

Naming/signature is entirely yours to decide (`on_turn_start` / `on_request` / a `turn_transform` that returns turns, etc.). The key need is a **safe, documented point to rewrite conversation history between tool rounds**.

### Alternatives considered

- `on_tool_result` + a captured `chat` to call `set_turns()`: works only by luck, is undocumented, doesn't fire without tools, and risks orphaning `tool_use`/`tool_result` pairs.
- Re-implementing the tool loop outside ellmer using lower-level primitives: `submit_turns()` is private, so there's no clean public way to drive one model turn + tools manually.

I'd be glad to send a PR if you're open to the feature — just let me know the API shape you'd prefer.

title: Feature Request: Allow custom `base_url` in `chat_google_vertex()` for API gateway proxies
description:
Note: Steps so far were run locally and final issue was created with assistance of Opus 4.6

## Problem

When using Google Vertex AI models through a corporate API gateway (Azure API Management),
the gateway proxies requests using Google's native API format
(`/v1beta1/publishers/google/models/{model}:generateContent`) with API key auth
(`x-goog-api-key` header).

Currently, `chat_google_vertex()` does not accept a `base_url` argument, so there's
no way to point it at a custom endpoint. The gateway is NOT OpenAI-compatible, so
`chat_openai_compatible()` doesn't work either.

## Workaround

Using `httr2` directly works:

```r
url <- "https://my-gateway.example.com/vertex-ai-express/v1beta1/publishers/google/models/gemini-2.5-flash-lite:generateContent"

resp <- request(url) |>
  req_headers(`x-goog-api-key` = api_key, `Content-Type` = "application/json") |>
  req_body_json(list(
    contents = list(list(role = "user", parts = list(list(text = "Hello!"))))
  )) |>
  req_perform()
```

The Python `google.genai` SDK supports this via `HttpOptions(base_url=...)`:

```python
from google.genai import Client
from google.genai.types import HttpOptions

client = Client(vertexai=True, api_key=api_key, http_options=HttpOptions(base_url=ENDPOINT))
```

## Proposed Solution
Add a `base_url` parameter to `chat_google_vertex()` that overrides the default Google endpoint URL, similar to how the Python SDK's `HttpOptions(base_url=...)` works.

This would also need to support API key authentication (via `x-goog-api-key header`) as an alternative to OAuth/service account credentials.

## Environment
* ellmer version: 0.4.1
* R version: [your R version]
* Gateway path format: /v1beta1/publishers/google/models/{model}:{method}
* Auth: x-goog-api-key header with API key

title: Feature request: public API to switch model/provider on an existing Chat while preserving conversation history
description:
## Problem

When building conversational agents on top of `ellmer`, there are common scenarios requiring the model to change mid-conversation while preserving the full turn history:

- **User-initiated model switch** (`/model opus` command while chatting)
- **Rate-limit fallback** (switch to a cheaper model when the primary hits limits)
- **Cost optimization** (downgrade from large to small model after a complex turn)
- **Debugging** (replay the same conversation against a different provider)

`Chat` currently exposes `get_provider()` (public read) but has no public write path for the provider or model. There is no `set_model()`, `set_provider()`, or `clone(provider=)`.

## What I am currently forced to do

```r
# Accessing the private R6 field directly -- the only working approach
.swap_provider <- function(chat, new_chat) {
  tryCatch({
    priv <- chat$.__enclos_env__$private
    if (is.null(priv) || is.null(priv$provider)) return(FALSE)
    priv$provider <- new_chat$get_provider()
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
}
```

This is fragile: it depends on the internal `private$provider` field name and the R6 `.__enclos_env__` accessor, both of which are implementation details that could change without notice.

## Empirical validation (13 points)

I tested several approaches before landing on the above hack:

| # | Test | Result |
|---|------|--------|
| 1 | Bare `set_turns()` migration | In-memory lossless, but **JSON serialization is lossy/fails** for tool turns |
| 2 | `contents_record/replay` | JSON-safe round-trip ✅ |
| 3 | Nested tool args + error results across providers | Fully lossless openai ↔ anthropic ✅ |
| 4 | `set_turns()` scope | Migrates turns only; **not** system_prompt or tools |
| 5 | Does ellmer have `set_model()`? | **No** -- but `provider@model` is an S7 mutable slot |
| 6 | `get_provider()` returns | A **copy** (mutating the copy does not write back) |
| 7 | Mutate `private$provider@model` | ✅ Same-provider model switch, turns intact |
| 8 | Replace entire `private$provider` | ✅ Cross-provider swap, turns+tools+system_prompt all preserved |
| 9 | Rebuild via `codeagent_client(new_chat)` | Turns preserved but all 50+ tools must be re-registered |
| 10 | Chat closures in Shiny modules | Chat is captured by 5 module functions; new object requires reactive indirection |
| 11 | `stream_controller` binding | Independent object, unaffected by provider swap ✅ |
| 12 | on_tool_result / on_tool_request callbacks | Registered on the Chat R6 object; survive in-place swap, broken on rebuild |
| 13 | System prompt re-injection | Required on rebuild (Route B); not needed on in-place swap (Route A) |

The core tension: **Route A** (in-place private mutation) keeps the Chat object identity — all registered callbacks, stream controllers, and Shiny module closures continue working untouched. **Route B** (rebuild via public API) is safer but requires re-registering 50+ tools, re-injecting the system prompt, and updating every closure that captured the old Chat object.

## Proposed API options (for maintainer discussion)

I see three reasonable public API shapes, in order of my preference:

**Option 1 — `chat$set_model(model)` (same-provider only)**

```r
chat$set_model("gpt-4o-mini")  # within the same provider
```

Safest: no cross-provider content incompatibilities. Covers the common case of downgrading within a vendor. A natural symmetric pair for `get_model()`.

**Option 2 — `chat$clone(provider = new_provider)` (immutable-friendly)**

```r
new_chat <- chat$clone(provider = chat_anthropic("claude-haiku-4-5")$get_provider())
```

Returns a new Chat with the same turns/tools/system_prompt but a different provider. Consistent with an immutable design philosophy. Caller is responsible for updating references.

**Option 3 — `chat$set_provider(provider)` (in-place, cross-provider)**

```r
chat$set_provider(chat_anthropic("claude-haiku-4-5")$get_provider())
```

Most powerful, but carries cross-provider semantic risk (different content block formats, tool schemas, thinking/reasoning representation). Could be offered with a disclaimer.

## My ask

1. Is there an intended public path I missed?
2. If this is a genuine API gap, which shape would you prefer to add?
3. If the answer is "use Route B / rebuild", is there a way to make that less painful (e.g. a `clone_with_turns(new_chat, source_chat)` helper)?

I am happy to submit a PR once there is maintainer agreement on the preferred shape, following the tidyverse PR workflow.

## Context

- ellmer 0.4.1
- Use case: [codeagent](https://github.com/kaipingyang/codeagent), an R-native coding agent harness built on ellmer
- Relevant internal file: `references/model-switch-alternatives.md` in codeagent (13-point test log)

title: DeepSeek tool calling can fail with as_json() error
description:
## DeepSeek tool calling can fail with `as_json()` error

When DeepSeek makes a tool call, `as_json()` can fail because `detect()` returns `NULL` and there's no method for `NULL`.

### Reprex

```r
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_deepseek(echo = "all")
chat$register_tool(tool(
  function() Sys.Date(),
  "Get the current date"
))
chat$chat("What's the current date in Y-M-D format?")
#> Error: Can't find method for generic `as_json(provider, x)`:
#> - provider: <ellmer::ProviderDeepSeek>
#> - x       : <NULL>
```

### Cause

In the [assistant turn branch of `as_json`](https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/blob/2370f315a1b4a3f1001f347eda7ed7651ef243f9/R/provider-deepseek.R#L116-L125), `detect()` is used to find a `ContentText`, which returns `NULL` when there is none, then passes it to `as_json()`:

```r
text <- detect(x@contents, S7_inherits, ContentText)
# ...
content = as_json(provider, text, ...),
```

The fix would be to filter contents (like [`ProviderOpenAICompatible`](https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/blob/2370f315a1b4a3f1001f347eda7ed7651ef243f9/R/provider-openai-compatible.R#L406-L422) does) rather than using `detect()`.

title: structured-data vignette should suggest a workaround when `.additional_properties` is unavailable
description:
The vignette currently notes that `.additional_properties = TRUE` in `type_object()` only works with Claude, not GPT, Gemini, or local models (Ollama):

> "This example only works with Claude, not GPT or Gemini, because only Claude supports adding additional, arbitrary properties."

It would be helpful to show a provider-agnostic workaround for the same open-ended extraction pattern — a `type_array` of key-value pair objects:

\`\`\`r
type_object(
  "All characteristics",
  traits = type_array(
    items = type_object(
      key   = type_string("trait name"),
      value = type_string("trait value")
    )
  )
)
\`\`\`

This works across all providers tested (OpenAI, Ollama, Gemini) and returns the same open-ended list of extracted properties, just as a tibble of `key`/`value` rows rather than named fields.

title: chat_openai() and chat_databricks(): param mappings are reversed in chat_params()
description:
Several `params()` arguments are silently ignored (with a warning) by `chat_openai()` and `chat_databricks()` because their `chat_params()` mappings have the API name and ellmer name swapped.

## Reprex

```r
chat <- chat_openai(params = params(max_tokens = 1))
chat$chat("tell me a limerick")
#> [full response, not truncated]
#> Warning message:
#> Ignoring unsupported parameters: "max_tokens"
```

## Cause

The convention in `standardise_params()` is `apiParamName = "ellmer_param_name"`. Two providers have mappings the wrong way round:

**`chat_openai()` (Responses API)** - 1 param affected:

```r
# Current (wrong)
max_tokens = "max_output_tokens"

# Should be
max_output_tokens = "max_tokens"
```

**`chat_databricks()`** - 4 params affected:

```r
# Current (wrong)
top_p = "topP",
top_k = "topK",
max_tokens = "maxTokens",
stop_sequences = "stopSequences"

# Should be
topP = "top_p",
topK = "top_k",
maxTokens = "max_tokens",
stopSequences = "stop_sequences"
```

Most other providers don't surface this bug because their API names and ellmer names are identical (e.g. `temperature = "temperature"`). Providers like Google and AWS that do have differing names (e.g. `maxOutputTokens = "max_tokens"`) have them the correct way round.

title: Tool definitions don't accept valid special characters for function names or arguments, such as "ñ"
description:
R functions that contain characters such as "ñ" (very common Spanish letter that produces a common problem in data science, as its used in the word _año_, meaning _year_) are completely valid in R, but they cause problems with `{ellmer}`

Lets create a basic function that has `ñ` in its name and in its argument:

```r
obtener_datos_por_año <- function(año = NULL) {
  
  require(dplyr)
  
  datos <- data.frame(
    año = c(2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024),
    inversión = c(100, 150, 200, 250, 300),
    proyectos = c(5, 8, 12, 15, 18)
  )
  
  datos <- datos |> 
    filter(año == .env$año)
  
  return(datos)
}
```
The function simply filters data from a dataframe.

Try out the function and it will work fine:

```r
obtener_datos_por_año(año = 2022)
```

Now let's create a tool definition with `{ellmer}`:

```r
library(ellmer)

# Crear la herramienta ellmer
tool_obtener_datos <- ellmer::tool(
  obtener_datos_por_año,
  "Obtiene datos de inversión y proyectos, filtrados opcionalmente por año (2020-2024)",
  arguments = list(
    año = type_integer(description = "Año a filtrar, entre 2020 y 2024")
  )
)
```

We get the first error: `ñ` is not supported in a function name:
```
# Error in `ellmer::tool()`:
#   ! `name` must contain only letters, numbers, - and _.
```

We have to change the function name (let´s say `anio` instead of `año`) to get rid of the error.

Now let's provide the LLM with the function definition:

```r
chat <- chat_anthropic(
  model = "claude-haiku-4-5"
)

chat$register_tool(tool_obtener_datos)
```

No problem so far, but let's ask a question that requires the model to use the tool, specifically the argument with `ñ` in its name:

```
chat$chat("muéstrame los proyectos de 2020") # "show me projects from 2020"
```

We get another `ñ` related error:
```
# Error in `req_perform_connection()`:
#   ! HTTP 400 Bad Request.
# ℹ tools.0.custom.input_schema.properties: Property keys should match
# pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,64}$' [invalid_request_error]
# Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.
```

I believe some cautions were taken to validate proper function and argument names in `{ellmer}` but those leave some users having to modify their work in order to match the english alphabet.

title: create_tool_def() always outputs english text, overwrites system prompt
description:
`create_tool_def()` sets its own system prompt in order to work, making it impossible to supply a system prompt when creating the chat() object required for `create_tool_def()` to work. Noticed this while struggling with `create_tool_def()` creating tool definitions in english, even when function and its documentation are in spanish. The system prompt used in `create_tool_def()`  translate to english the original roxygen2 comments describing the function and its arguments.

While I understand english is a more optimized language for LLMs, for production systems we try to avoid all english to minimize the possibilities of an LLM suddenly defaulting to english text after reading a tool definition in said language.

title: Write path serializes thinking as reasoning_content which some providers don't support
description:
In #981, reasoning effort was enabled for Ollama, which also updated the read path to check both `reasoning` and `reasoning_content` fields.

However, when `preserve_thinking = TRUE`, the multi-turn write path in `ProviderOpenAICompatible` serializes `ContentThinking` back as `reasoning_content`. Providers like vLLM only recognize `reasoning` (removed `reasoning_content` entirely in vllm-project/vllm#33402).

The ecosystem is split on field naming:

- OpenAI and OpenRouter recommend `reasoning` as primary (with `reasoning_content` as alias)
- LM Studio uses only `reasoning_content`
- vLLM uses only `reasoning`

One option is a field on `ProviderOpenAICompatible` to configure which field name to use. See discussion in #981 for more context.

Not currently biting anyone since `preserve_thinking` defaults to `FALSE` for Ollama, but worth addressing.

title: chat$get_cost() returns NA for Gemini 3.5 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite models

response

chat$get_cost()

chat$get_tokens()
```

`chat$get_cost()` returns:

```r
[1] NA

title: Bearer Token / API Key Authentication for chat_aws_bedrock()
description:
Hi Hadley, just ran into the issue that I couldn't natively request our internal Bedrock endpoints which rely on Bearer Token authentication (API key via `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header, no SigV4 signing). I built a workaround using httr2 as a proof of concept, but of course I'm losing all ellmer features like streaming, tool calling, etc. Is this something that could be resolved on the ellmer side? I believe it has quite some impact for enterprise users behind API gateways. Let me know in case you need any further info.

### Problem
`chat_aws_bedrock()` requires IAM credentials via `paws.common`, which doesn't support the **Bearer Token authentication** that AWS Bedrock launched in July 2025. This prevents users who access Bedrock through enterprise API gateways (which issue API keys instead of IAM credentials) from using `ellmer` natively.

### Reproduction

```r
Sys.setenv(AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK = "my-api-key")

chat <- chat_aws_bedrock(
  base_url = "https://my-company-gateway.example.com/bedrock",
  model = "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0"
)
# Error: No IAM credentials found.
```

Python's boto3 supports this via `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` — it skips SigV4 signing and sends `Authorization: Bearer <key>` instead.

### Proposal
Add a `credentials` parameter (similar to `chat_azure_openai()`) that, when provided:

1. Skips `paws.common` IAM credential resolution
2. Sends the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` header
3. Does not apply SigV4 signing

```r
# Desired API
chat <- chat_aws_bedrock(
  base_url = "https://my-company-gateway.example.com/bedrock",
  model = "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0",
  credentials = "my-api-key"
)
```

### Workaround
Currently requires calling the Bedrock Converse API directly via `httr2`, losing all `ellmer` features (streaming, tool calling, `parallel_chat()`, etc.).

title: Google Vertex authentication flow fails upon finding GOOGLE_API_KEY env var
description:
Noticed this today when testing things on another PR.  

``` r
library(ellmer)
chat <- chat_google_vertex(
  location = Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION"),
  project_id = Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT"),
  model = "gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview", params = params(reasoning_tokens = 1024)
)
chat$chat("What's 2+2")
#> Error in `req_perform_connection()`:
#> ! HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
#> • OAuth error
#> • realm: https://accounts.google.com/
#> ℹ API keys are not supported by this API. Expected OAuth2 access token or other
#>   authentication credentials that assert a principal. See
#>   https://cloud.google.com/docs/authentication

Sys.unsetenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY")
chat <- chat_google_vertex(
  location = Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION"),
  project_id = Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT"),
  model = "gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview", params = params(reasoning_tokens = 1024)
)
#> Warning: Unable to refresh token: invalid_grant
#> reauth related error (invalid_rapt)
#> https://support.google.com/a/answer/9368756
chat$chat("What's 2+2")
#> Error in `if (expiry < Sys.time()) ...`:
#> ! argument is of length zero
```

<sup>Created on 2026-05-22 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>


*Issue 1 - checking for API key existence*

Firstly, `default_google_credentials()` checks `GOOGLE_API_KEY` regardless of variant, and so when I have it set and call `chat_google_vertex()` it tries to send the API key even though I want 0Auth2.  

As `chat_google_vertex()` doesn't expose `credentials` or `api_key`, we can just skip this block in `default_google_credentials()`. 

(N.B. Google Vertex, which appears to be rebranded to Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, [doesn't allow for using API keys except for in express mode](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/reference/express-mode/api-reference), which we don't implement here - there may be a case for doing so, but beyond the scope of this ticket)

*Issue 2 - checking for API key existence*

The second example actually was a workaround which did work, but failed when I switched IDEs and may have surfaced another bug.  

Claude description:

> "After unsetting `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `gargle::token_fetch()` tries to use cached credentials that need refreshing. The refresh fails with "invalid_grant", but gargle still returns the token (not NULL) in a bad state. Since token$can_refresh() is TRUE, we hit the final branch where expiry is computed from token$credentials$expires_in — but that's NULL after the failed refresh, so expiry becomes numeric(0). The subsequent `if (expiry < Sys.time())` then errors with "argument is of length zero". 

> The root cause is a stale gargle token cache, but ellmer should handle this more gracefully (e.g. defaulting expires_in to 0 when NULL, so it forces an immediate refresh attempt)"

I'm thinking we want something like:

```r
if (!is.null(token) && is.null(token$credentials$access_token)) {                                                           
      cli::cli_abort(c(
                                                                                                                                
    "Google credentials were found but are not valid.",
    "i" = "Run {.code gcloud auth application-default login} to set up                                                          
    application default credentials."                                                                                           
    ))
  }
```

but without assuming the user is going to be using `gcloud` command line, so perhaps more generic.

We might also want to check for the existence of `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION` and `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` for `chat_google_vertex()`, or just set the default location/project param values to these env vars? In #434, it looks like the reason we don't have them as default is because there was nothing in the docs indicating this, but now there's https://docs.cloud.google.com/workflows/docs/reference/environment-variables

title: Support adaptive thinking with Claude via `params()`
description:
Currently, with Claude, `params = list(reasoning_effort)` is unsupported:

```r
ch <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-4-6", params = list(reasoning_effort = "high"))
ch$chat("Write a limerick about dplyr")
#> Warning: Ignoring unsupported parameters: "reasoning_effort"
#> ...
```

Older Claude models used "Extended Thinking", which took a token budget, which is the interface that ellmer currently supports. Newer Claude releases have transitioned to "Adaptive Thinking" which takes a reasoning _effort_.

To use it, we need to set `thinking.type` and `output_config.effort`, like:

```r
ch <- chat_claude(
  model = "claude-sonnet-4-6", 
  api_args = list(
    thinking = list(type = "adaptive"), 
    output_config = list(effort = "high")
  )
)
ch$chat("Write a limerick about dplyr")
```

More on which models support which thinking interface and the various API shapes: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/adaptive-thinking

Could we allow instead setting `reasoning_effort` for the models that support adaptive thinking?

```r
ch <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-4-6", params = list(reasoning_effort = "high"))
```

### 🤖 explanation  

`chat_structured()` passes `stream = echo != "none"` to `submit_turns()`, which uses streaming mode in `chat_perform()`. But some providers override `stream <- FALSE` in `chat_body()` (e.g. the Anthropic tool-based structured output path).  This creates a mismatch: the client expects a streaming response but the API returns a regular JSON response.

The mismatch: `chat_perform()` picks the `"stream"` branch based on the mode argument, but `chat_body()` has already set `stream: false` in the request body.  The API returns a non-streaming response, but the client tries to parse it as a stream.

title: Streaming ContentThinking chunks lack proper <thinking> tag boundaries
description:
## Current behavior

When streaming with `stream = "content"`, each `ContentThinking` chunk is yielded as an independent object. If you print or concatenate these (via `format()`), each fragment gets its own `<thinking>...</thinking>` wrapper:

```r
chat <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514")

stream <- chat$stream("Explain recursion", stream = "content")
coro::loop(for (chunk in stream) {
  cat(format(chunk))
})
```

Output:

```
<thinking>
The user wants an explanation
</thinking>
<thinking>
 of recursion. I should
</thinking>
<thinking>
 start with a simple definition...
</thinking>
Recursion is a technique where...
```

With `stream = "text"`, thinking text is yielded as bare strings indistinguishable from response text:

```r
stream <- chat$stream("Explain recursion", stream = "text")
coro::loop(for (chunk in stream) {
  cat(chunk)
})
```

Output:

```
The user wants an explanation of recursion. I should start with a simple definition...Recursion is a technique where...
```

No way to tell where thinking ended and the response began.

## Expected behavior

The streaming layer should emit `<thinking>` tags at the boundaries — once at the start of thinking, once at the end — so that concatenated output is well-formed:

For `stream = "text"`:
```
<thinking>
The user wants an explanation of recursion. I should start with a simple definition...
</thinking>

Recursion is a technique where...
```

For `stream = "content"`, the yielded objects stay the same (`ContentThinking` per chunk), but the echo/display output should show proper boundaries.

## Why this matters

Downstream consumers (like shinychat) that receive a stream and need to separate thinking from response content currently have to implement their own stateful tracking of `ContentThinking` objects, accumulate the thinking text, and reconstruct the tag boundaries themselves. If the stream already had correct boundaries in text mode, consumers could treat it as a text stream with well-formed `<thinking>` tags and parse accordingly — no type inspection needed.

title: Token Budget / Cap for Agentic Tool Call Loops
description:
**Describe the problem**
When running unsupervised/scheduled agentic workflows that involve tool calls, there is currently no built-in way to enforce an upper token limit on the full multi-turn loop. Without this, a runaway loop can consume far more tokens than intended with no mechanism to stop it gracefully.

**Desired behavior**
It would be useful to have a supported way to:
1. Set a hard token budget for the entire tool call loop, causing it to stop (and error/fail gracefully) if the limit is exceeded.
2. Optionally inject a system-level message (e.g. *"You are approaching your token limit — wrap up your response now"*) once a soft threshold is reached, giving the model a chance to return a partial result rather than hard-stopping.

**Use case**
Unsupervised scheduled reports with tool access, where cost/token control is a requirement to prevent silent runaway.

title: parallel_chat and parallel_chat_structured return different outputs shapes
description:
## Summary

`parallel_chat()` and `parallel_chat_structured()` currently return different kinds of objects:

- `parallel_chat()` returns a list of `Chat` objects, `NULL`s, or error objects
- `parallel_chat_structured()` returns a structured data object, typically a data frame

This makes downstream code more complex than it needs to be, because callers have to branch on which function they used and handle two different result shapes.

## Why this matters

The two functions are very close in intent:
- both submit multiple prompts in parallel
- both can fail on individual rows
- both may need per-row recovery logic

But because the return shapes differ, callers cannot treat them as drop-in alternatives.

That makes it harder to:
- write generic post-processing
- salvage parse failures
- retry only failing rows
- keep uniform logging and metadata handling

## Proposed direction

A more uniform design would be for both functions to return a list of `Chat` objects, with the raw assistant text preserved even when structured parsing fails.

For `parallel_chat_structured()`, that would mean:
- returning the raw unprocessed string on parse failure
- keeping enough metadata to allow ad hoc parsing or recovery later
- not collapsing the result directly into a data frame too early

That way callers could inspect and salvage failed turns instead of losing the raw output.

## Even better

An even cleaner API would be to let `parallel_chat()` accept an optional `type` argument:
- if `type` is absent, return normal chat outputs
- if `type` is present, return structured outputs

That would make the structured and unstructured paths true drop-ins with a single entry point.

## Example

A model such as:

https://openrouter.ai/openai/gpt-oss-20b:free

can return JSON-like output that is close to valid but not always perfectly parseable. In those cases, preserving the raw string would let callers recover the response with custom parsing logic.

title: Add prompt caching support to `chat_aws_bedrock()`
description:
AWS Bedrock's Converse API now supports prompt caching via [`CachePointBlock`](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_CachePointBlock.html) objects. This works for both Anthropic Claude and Amazon Nova models. We should add a `cache` parameter to `chat_aws_bedrock()` to take advantage of this, following the same pattern used by `chat_anthropic()`.

PR #939 proposed a separate `chat_bedrock_anthropic()` provider using the InvokeModel API (Anthropic Messages format) to enable caching. However, since the Converse API now supports caching natively, we can add this directly to `chat_aws_bedrock()` without needing a second provider or Anthropic-specific API surface.

## How Bedrock Converse API caching works

Full docs: <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html>

> You can use prompt caching anytime you get model inference in Amazon Bedrock for supported models. Prompt caching is supported by the following Amazon Bedrock features:
>
> **Converse and ConverseStream APIs**
>
> You can carry on a conversation with a model where you specify cache checkpoints in your prompts.
>
> **InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream APIs**
>
> You can submit single prompt requests in which you enable prompt caching and specify your cache checkpoints.

> When using prompt caching, you're charged at a reduced rate for tokens read from cache. Depending on the model, tokens written to cache may be charged at a rate that is higher than that of uncached input tokens. Any tokens not read from or written to cache, are charged at the standard input token rate for that model. For more information, see the [Amazon Bedrock pricing page](https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/).

### CachePointBlock

Cache points are placed as content blocks in three locations: `system`, `messages`, and `tools`. The block structure is:

```json
{
  "cachePoint": {
    "type": "default",
    "ttl": "5m"
  }
}
```

`ttl` is optional (defaults to 5-minute caching). Valid values are `"5m"` and `"1h"`. 1-hour TTL is only supported by Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Haiku 4.5, and Claude Sonnet 4.5.


### Placement examples

**System prompt:**
```json
"system": [
  {"text": "You are a helpful assistant..."},
  {"cachePoint": {"type": "default"}}
]
```

**Messages (last content block in last turn):**
```json
"messages": [
  {
    "role": "user",
    "content": [
      {"text": "Analyze this data..."},
      {"cachePoint": {"type": "default"}}
    ]
  }
]
```

**Tools:**
```json
"toolConfig": {
  "tools": [
    {"toolSpec": { ... }},
    {"cachePoint": {"type": "default"}}
  ]
}
```

> For Claude models, Amazon Bedrock offers a simplified approach to cache management that reduces the complexity of manually placing cache checkpoints. Instead of requiring you to specify exact cache checkpoint locations, you can use automatic cache management with a single breakpoint at the end of your static content.
> 
> When you enable simplified cache management, the system automatically checks for cache hits at previous content block boundaries, looking back up to approximately 20 content blocks from your specified breakpoint. This allows the model to find the longest matching prefix from your cache without requiring you to predict the optimal checkpoint locations. To use this, place a single cache checkpoint at the end of your static content, before any dynamic or variable content. The system will automatically find the best cache match.


### Constraints

- Maximum **4 cache checkpoints** per request.
- Minimum token thresholds vary by model (1,024 for most Claude models, 2,048 for Claude 3.5 Haiku, 4,096 for Claude Opus 4.5/Haiku 4.5). Below the threshold, inference succeeds but content is not cached.
- Longer TTL entries must appear before shorter TTL entries in the same request.

> "Cache hits are not deducted against your rate limit."

### Response fields

The Converse API response includes:

- `CacheReadInputTokens` — tokens read from cache
- `CacheWriteInputTokens` — tokens written to cache
- `CacheDetails` — the TTL used for tokens written to cache

### Pricing

> "When using prompt caching, you're charged at a reduced rate for tokens read from cache. Depending on the model, tokens written to cache may be charged at a rate that is higher than that of uncached input tokens."

Same general structure as Anthropic direct: writes cost more, reads cost less, net savings on multi-turn conversations with large system prompts.

### Supported models

All current Anthropic Claude models on Bedrock, plus Amazon Nova Micro/Lite/Pro/Premier/Nova 2 Lite.

## Open questions

### Behavior of `cachePoint` on unsupported models

The docs confirm that for supported models, if the content is below the minimum token threshold, "your inference will still succeed, but your prefix will not be cached." However, the docs are silent on what happens if a `cachePoint` block is sent to a model that **does not support caching at all** (e.g., an older model or a third-party model on Bedrock). It may be silently ignored or it may cause a validation error.

This needs to be tested before deciding on the default value for `cache`. If unsupported models ignore the block, we can safely default to `"5m"` (matching `chat_anthropic()`). If they error, we should either default to `"none"` or gate caching on a list of known-supported models.

## Recommended approach

### 1. Add `cache` parameter to `chat_aws_bedrock()`

Follow the same interface as `chat_anthropic()`: `cache = c("5m", "1h", "none")`, defaulting to `"5m"`. Add a `cache` property to `ProviderAWSBedrock`.

### 2. Insert cache points in `chat_request()`

In the `chat_request()` method for `ProviderAWSBedrock`, append a `cachePoint` block:

- After the system prompt text block (in the `system` list)
- After the last content block of the last message turn (in `messages`)

This mirrors how `chat_body()` in `ProviderAnthropic` adds `cache_control` to the system prompt and the last content block of the last turn.

A helper like `bedrock_cache_point()` (analogous to the existing `cache_control()` helper in `provider-claude.R`) could return `NULL` when caching is disabled or the appropriate `list(cachePoint = list(type = "default", ttl = ttl))` otherwise.

### 3. Update `value_tokens()` for cache tracking

The current `value_tokens()` for `ProviderAWSBedrock` only tracks `inputTokens` and `outputTokens`. Update it to also report `cached_input` from the response's `CacheReadInputTokens`, and fold `CacheWriteInputTokens` into the input cost (same approach as `ProviderAnthropic`).

### 4. Tests, docs, NEWS

- Add tests for caching (at minimum: verify cache point blocks appear in the request body).
- Update `chat_aws_bedrock()` docs to describe the `cache` parameter and link to the AWS caching docs.
- Add NEWS.md entry.

title: Support multi-turn conversation suffixes in `parallel_chat_structured()`
description:
### Problem

`parallel_chat_structured()` currently supports only a single user turn per parallel job. This is because `as_user_turns()` converts each element of `prompts` into one `UserTurn`, and `append_turns()` appends that single turn to the shared conversation history:

```r
# R/parallel-chat.R L192-199
user_turns <- as_user_turns(prompts)
existing <- chat$get_turns(include_system_prompt = TRUE)
conversations <- append_turns(list(existing), user_turns)
```

```r
# R/turns.R L219-231
as_user_turns <- function(prompts, ...) {
  turns <- map(seq_along(prompts), function(i) {
    as_user_turn(prompts[[i]], ...)
  })
  turns
}
```

There is no mechanism to supply a multi-turn conversation suffix (e.g., user → assistant → user) per parallel job. Workloads that require each parallel item to be its own short conversation — rather than a single prompt — must fall back to sequential `chat$chat_structured()` calls on separate `Chat` objects, losing the throughput benefit of the parallel API.

### Use case

Simulation-style and survey-style workflows where each parallel item naturally involves multiple turns before the structured extraction. For example, running 500 independent two-turn conversations in parallel:

- **Turn 1:** establish identity/context for a simulated respondent
- **Turn 2:** ask the rating/classification question
- **Return:** structured JSON response

Other examples include multi-step annotation pipelines and interview-style prompting where the model should condition on a short prior exchange before producing a structured answer.

### Proposed API

Allow each element of `prompts` to be either a string (current behaviour, one turn) or a list of strings (new, multi-turn suffix):

```r
parallel_chat_structured(
  chat = chat,
  prompts = list(
    # Job 1: two-turn conversation
    list("You are simulating a Democrat.", "Rate this statement from 0 to 100."),
    # Job 2: two-turn conversation
    list("You are simulating a Republican.", "Rate this statement from 0 to 100."),
    # Job 3: single-turn (backward compatible)
    "Rate this statement from 0 to 100."
  ),
  type = response_type
)
```

This would also apply to `parallel_chat()`, `parallel_chat_text()`, and `batch_chat_structured()` since they share the same `as_user_turns()` / `append_turns()` pipeline.

### Implementation notes

The main changes would likely be in:

- **`as_user_turns()`** (`R/turns.R`): detect when an element is a list of strings and return a list of `Turn` objects (alternating user/assistant) rather than a single `UserTurn`.
- **`append_turns()`** (`R/parallel-chat.R`): handle appending a sequence of turns rather than a single turn.
- **`parallel_chat_structured()`** (`R/parallel-chat.R`): the structured variant would need to issue multiple rounds of `parallel_turns()` calls, similar to how `parallel_chat()` already loops for tool calls.

### Not a bug

The current docs and API clearly treat `prompts` as single-turn inputs. This is a feature request to extend the parallel API to cover multi-turn workloads.

_Originally raised in https://github.com/rempsyc/ellmer/issues/4._

title: Enhancement: Retry on HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout (Portkey and similar providers)
description:
## Summary

Some LLM API providers (including Portkey AI Gateway) may occasionally return HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout errors, especially when chained behind additional reverse proxies (e.g., in university or enterprise deployments). By default, ellmer retries on 429 and 503, but **not** on 504, which also represents a classic transient error.

## Details

- The NYU GenAI gateway (`ai-gateway.apps.cloud.rt.nyu.edu`) sometimes sends a 504, even though the downstream model eventually responds with 200 after e.g. 94 seconds (see [rempsyc/ellmer#3](https://github.com/rempsyc/ellmer/issues/3) for logs).
- The ellmer Portkey provider currently passes `is_transient` as NULL to `ellmer_req_robustify()`, meaning only 429 and 503 are retried (httr2 default).
- This causes ~45% failure rates for long model runs, with no client-side recovery.

## Recommendation

**Patch suggestion:**

```r
# In R/provider-portkey.R (and/or via an argument to ellmer_req_robustify, as appropriate)
method(base_request, ProviderPortkeyAI) <- function(provider) {
  req <- request(provider@base_url)

  req <- ellmer_req_credentials(
    req,
    provider@credentials(),
    "x-portkey-api-key"
  )
  req <- ellmer_req_robustify(req, is_transient = function(resp) {
    resp_status(resp) %in% c(429, 503, 504)
  })
  req <- ellmer_req_user_agent(req)
  req <- base_request_error(provider, req)
  req
}
```

Alternatively, consider adding 504 to the default retryable errors for all providers.

## Upstream rationale

- 504 is transient and common in multi-proxy situations or slow generative models
- This change is unlikely to break existing users, as retries are bounded by `max_tries` (default 3)

## References
- [Portkey request timeouts documentation](https://docs.portkey.ai/docs/product/ai-gateway/request-timeouts) — Portkey does not impose a default timeout; the 504 originates from an upstream reverse proxy.
- https://github.com/rempsyc/ellmer/issues/3 (full diagnostics and logs)

title: Not possible to pass `think = FALSE` to Ollama models via `chat_ollama()`
description:
I’m using `chat_ollama()` with a local Ollama model (`qwen3.5:4b`). Ollama allows to [disable reasoning](https://ollama.com/blog/thinking) for thinking models using the `think = false` parameter (CLI flag `--think=false`). The provided Python code works. However, I haven’t found a way to pass this parameter through `chat_ollama()` with ellmer. 

From looking at the implementation, it seems that:

* `chat_ollama()` uses the OpenAI-compatible API (`/v1/chat/completions`).
* The `chat_params()` method for `ProviderOllama` maps only a limited set of parameters (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, etc.):

```r
method(chat_params, ProviderOllama) <- function(provider, params) {
  standardise_params(
    params,
    c(
      frequency_penalty = "frequency_penalty",
      presence_penalty = "presence_penalty",
      seed = "seed",
      stop = "stop_sequences",
      temperature = "temperature",
      top_p = "top_p",
      top_k = "top_k",
      max_tokens = "max_tokens"
    )
  )
}
```

I added `think = "think"` locally to the package and re-installed it, but that did not change anything. I also tried passing the argument via `api_args`:

```r
chat <- chat_ollama(
  model = "qwen3.5:4b",
  api_args = list(think = FALSE)
)
```

but this also does not seem to propagate the parameter to the Ollama request.

Is there currently a supported way to pass `think = FALSE` to Ollama models when using `chat_ollama()` or is this limitation due to using the OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of the native Ollama API?

title: Example code to generate WAV audio from text using Gemini TTS and present it in a Shiny audio preview modal
description:
This issue provides working example code to generate WAV audio from text using Gemini TTS and present it in a Shiny audio preview modal.

### Example Code
```r
options(ellmer_timeout_s = 900) # for long audio

gemini_tts = function(text, voice="charon", model="gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts", api_key=NULL) {
  api_key = api_key %||% Sys.getenv("GOOGLE_API_KEY")
  if (is.null(api_key) || api_key == "") {
    stop("Google API key not found. Set GOOGLE_API_KEY or pass api_key as a parameter.")
  }
  # Internal function to create a WAV header from raw PCM
  create_wav_header = function(data_length, sample_rate = 24000, bits_per_sample = 16, channels = 1) {
    byte_rate <- sample_rate * channels * bits_per_sample / 8
    block_align <- channels * bits_per_sample / 8
    header <- raw(44)
    # "RIFF" chunk
    header[1:4] <- charToRaw("RIFF")
    size <- data_length + 36
    header[5:8] <- writeBin(as.integer(size), raw(), size = 4, endian = "little")
    header[9:12] <- charToRaw("WAVE")
    # "fmt " subchunk
    header[13:16] <- charToRaw("fmt ")
    header[17:20] <- writeBin(16L, raw(), size = 4, endian = "little")
    header[21:22] <- writeBin(1L, raw(), size = 2, endian = "little")
    header[23:24] <- writeBin(as.integer(channels), raw(), size = 2, endian = "little")
    header[25:28] <- writeBin(as.integer(sample_rate), raw(), size = 4, endian = "little")
    header[29:32] <- writeBin(as.integer(byte_rate), raw(), size = 4, endian = "little")
    header[33:34] <- writeBin(as.integer(block_align), raw(), size = 2, endian = "little")
    header[35:36] <- writeBin(as.integer(bits_per_sample), raw(), size = 2, endian = "little")
    # "data" subchunk
    header[37:40] <- charToRaw("data")
    header[41:44] <- writeBin(as.integer(data_length), raw(), size = 4, endian = "little")
    header
  }
  # Build URL
  base_url = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models"
  url = paste0(base_url, "/", model, ":generateContent")
  # Create and execute request
  req = httr2::request(url) |>
    httr2::req_url_query(key = api_key) |>
    httr2::req_timeout(60*15) |>
    httr2::req_body_json(list(
      contents = list(list(
        parts = list(list(text = text))
      )),
      generationConfig = list(
        responseModalities = list("AUDIO"),
        speechConfig = list(
          voiceConfig = list(
            prebuiltVoiceConfig = list(
              voiceName = voice
            )
          )
        )
      )
    ))
  resp = httr2::req_perform(req)
  json_resp = httr2::resp_body_json(resp)
  # Extract base64 audio
  audio_base64 = json_resp$candidates[[1]]$content$parts[[1]]$inlineData$data
  if (is.null(audio_base64)) {
    stop("No audio received from the API response")
  }
  # Decode and create WAV
  audio_pcm  = base64enc::base64decode(audio_base64)
  wav_header = create_wav_header(length(audio_pcm))
  # Return complete raw WAV
  c(wav_header, audio_pcm)
}

  shiny::modalDialog(
    title = title,

    easyClose = TRUE,
    bslib::card(

        style = "background-color: #000000; color: #e0e0e0;",
        shiny::tags$audio(

          style = "width: 100%;",
          shiny::tags$source(

        ),
        shiny::tags$hr(),
        shiny::tags$p(class = "text-muted", "If the audio doesn't start, press Play.")

}

```

title: parallel_chat_structured() errors with chat_aws_bedrock() due to double vs integer token counts
description:
The code below fails when setting `include_tokens=TRUE` or `include_cost=TRUE` due to results being returned as doubles where integers are expected. This issue appears to be unique to AWS Bedrock models, as `chat_anthropic()` does not have this error.

```
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_aws_bedrock(model = "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6")

prompts <- list(
  "Extract the person's name and age: 'My name is Alex and I am 30 years old.'",
  "Extract the person's name and age: 'I'm Jordan, age 25.'"
)

type_person <- type_object(
  name = type_string("The person's name."),
  age  = type_integer("The person's age.")
)

# Errors with:
#
# Error in `vapply()`:
# ! values must be type 'integer',
#  but FUN(X[[1]]) result is type 'double'
# Backtrace:
#  1. ellmer::parallel_chat_structured(...)
#  2. ellmer:::multi_convert(...)
#  3. base::t(vapply(turns, function(turn) turn@tokens, integer(3)))
#  4. base::vapply(turns, function(turn) turn@tokens, integer(3))
result <- parallel_chat_structured(
  chat    = chat,
  prompts = prompts,
  type    = type_person,
  include_tokens = TRUE,
  include_cost = TRUE
)
```

title: chat_databricks(): HTTP 400 when conversation history contains empty ContentText
description:
## Problem

When the conversation history contains a `ContentText("")` (empty text), `chat_databricks()` fails with HTTP 400 because the Databricks Claude proxy rejects empty text content blocks.

This can happen organically during tool calling when a model responds with tool calls and an empty `content` field (`content: ""` instead of `content: null`). When ellmer replays the conversation history on the next round-trip, the serialized empty text block `{"type": "text", "text": ""}` is rejected.

## Reprex

```r
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_databricks(model = "databricks-claude-sonnet-4-5")

# Simulate what happens when the model returns content = "" during tool calling
chat$set_turns(list(
  UserTurn(list(ContentText("Hello"))),
  AssistantTurn(list(ContentText("")))
))

# Fails because the empty text content block is serialized as
# {"type": "text", "text": ""} which Databricks rejects
chat$chat("How are you?", echo = "none")
#> Error in `req_perform()`:
#> ! HTTP 400 Bad Request.
#> ℹ {"message":"messages: text content blocks must be non-empty"}
```

## Root cause

This is a Databricks-specific double problem:

1. **Databricks returns `content: ""` in responses** for tool-only turns (instead of `content: null` which OpenAI returns). This causes `value_turn()` for `ProviderOpenAICompatible` (`R/provider-openai-compatible.R:290`) to create `ContentText("")`:

```r
content <- lapply(message$content, as_content)
# lapply("", as_content) → ContentText("") since as_content() doesn't validate non-empty strings
```

2. **Databricks then rejects `content: ""` when replayed back** → HTTP 400.

Other OpenAI-compatible providers (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI) return `content: null` for tool-only turns, so `lapply(NULL, as_content)` → `list()` and no empty `ContentText` is ever created. Databricks creates the problem and then rejects it.

## Possible fixes

1. **Filter in `value_turn()`**: Drop empty `ContentText` when parsing model responses
2. **Filter in `as_json()`**: Skip empty `ContentText` during serialization (similar to the existing empty assistant turn check in `provider-claude.R:418-422`)
3. **Validate in `ContentText`**: Reject empty strings at construction time (breaking change)

title: Tool call escapes the JSON string
description:
_The following example tries to provide full context demonstrating the issues. The bug not always shows due to the unexpected nature of AI agent._

  Reproduces a bug where qwen3-coder:30b on Ollama wraps every tool string
  argument in JSON array brackets:

    Expected: write_file(path = "SKILL.md", content = "hello")
    Actual:   write_file(path = '["SKILL.md"]', content = '["hello"]')

  This makes all tool calls fail when the tool validates its inputs.

  Root cause: The MODEL generates malformed tool call arguments.
  Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API faithfully passes them through,
  and ellmer's ProviderOpenAICompatible does not coerce array→string.

  Question: should ellmer unwrap single-element arrays when the
  tool schema declares type_string()? Although `'["SKILL.md"]'` is also a string, the model may go crazy into escaping strings (sometimes `'\\\\[\\\\\\\\"SKILL.md\\\\\\\\"\\\\]'` after several failed attempts.)

  Prerequisites:
    - Ollama running at the URL below
    - Model: ollama pull qwen3-coder:30b


``` r

# test-ollama-array-wrap-bug.R
# ====================================================================


library(ellmer)

ollama_url <- "http://127.0.0.1:11434"

chat <- chat_ollama(
  base_url = ollama_url,
  model = "qwen3-coder:30b",
  system_prompt = paste(
    "You are a file-writing assistant.",
    "When asked to create a file, use the write_file tool.",
    "Do NOT ask questions. Just write the file.",
    "IMPORTANT! DO NOT CALL TOOLS IN PARALLEL; ALWAYS CALL THEM IN SEQUENTIAL ORDER: THE PLATFORM YOU ARE RUNNING ON CRASHES/SEGFAULTS WITH PARALLEL TOOL CALLS.",
    "/nothink"
  )
)

# --- Tool that logs what it receives ---
received_args <- list()

write_file_tool <- tool(
  function(path, content) {
    received_args$path <<- path
    received_args$content <<- content
    cat("\n=== write_file CALLED ===\n")
    cat("  path type:  ", typeof(path), "\n")
    cat("  path value: ", repr::repr(path), "\n")
    if (grepl("^\\[", path)) {
      stop(sprintf("BUG: path wrapped in array brackets: %s", path))
    }
    paste0("File written: ", path)
  },
  name = "write_file",
  description = "Write content to a file at the given path. Use RELATIVE paths only.",
  arguments = list(
    path = type_string("Relative file path to write to.", required = TRUE),
    content = type_string("The text content to write.", required = TRUE)
  )
)

read_file_tool <- tool(
  function(path) {
    cat("\n=== read_file CALLED ===\n")
    cat("  path value: ", repr::repr(path), "\n")
    if (grepl("^\\[", path)) {
      stop(sprintf("BUG: path wrapped in array brackets: %s", path))
    }
    "name: example\ndescription: An example skill."
  },
  name = "read_file",
  description = "Read a file at the given relative path.",
  arguments = list(
    path = type_string("Relative file path to read.", required = TRUE)
  )
)

walk_dir_tool <- tool(
  function(path) {
    cat("\n=== walk_directory CALLED ===\n")
    cat("  path value: ", repr::repr(path), "\n")

      required = FALSE
    )
  )
)

chat$register_tool(write_file_tool)
chat$register_tool(read_file_tool)
chat$register_tool(walk_dir_tool)

# --- Trigger the bug with a multi-step prompt ---

title: Feature request: unwrap single-element arrays as a defensive measure
description:
With multiple tools, ollama models merges all tool names into one garbled call (see below): walk_directorywrite_filewrite_filewrite_file() — it concatenates all the tool names together and sends them as a single malformed tool request.

It's a model bug — qwen3-coder:30b doesn't properly format multi-tool calls in the OpenAI-compatible format. There are actually two separate issues:

Merged tool names: When the model wants to call multiple tools, it concatenates them into one string instead of separate tool_calls entries
Array-wrapped arguments: When it does call individual tools (after error retry), it wraps string values in ["..."] (in the function call: this is a separate issue and I'm still trying to figure it out/find a stable repreducible reprex)
Both are model-level issues with how qwen3-coder:30b serializes tool calls through Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API. ellmer can't reasonably fix malformed tool names being concatenated. The ["..."] array wrapping could theoretically be mitigated in ellmer by unwrapping single-element arrays when the schema says type_string().

I don't think this is an ellmer bug since ellmer faithfully implements the API but Ollama API becomes unusable since its parser allows this format.


``` r
# ====================================================================
# test-ollama-array-wrap-bug.R
# ====================================================================
# Reproduces a bug where qwen3-coder:30b wraps every tool string
# argument in JSON array brackets:
#
#   Expected: write_file(path = "SKILL.md", content = "hello")
#   Actual:   write_file(path = '["SKILL.md"]', content = '["hello"]')
#
# This makes all tool calls fail when the tool validates its inputs.
#
# Root cause: The MODEL generates malformed tool call arguments.
# Ollama's OpenAI-compatible API faithfully passes them through,
# and ellmer's ProviderOpenAICompatible does not coerce array→string.
#
# Question: should ellmer unwrap single-element arrays when the
# tool schema declares type_string()?
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - Ollama running at the URL below
#   - Model: ollama pull qwen3-coder:30b
# ====================================================================

library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_ollama(
  model = "qwen3-coder:30b",
  system_prompt = paste(
    "You are a file-writing assistant.",
    "When asked to create a file, use the write_file tool.",
    "Do NOT ask questions. Just write the file.",
    "/nothink"
  )
)

# --- Tool that logs what it receives ---
received_args <- list()

write_file_tool <- tool(
  function(path, content) {
    received_args$path <<- path
    received_args$content <<- content
    cat("\n=== write_file CALLED ===\n")
    cat("  path type:  ", typeof(path), "\n")
    cat("  path value: ", repr::repr(path), "\n")
    if (grepl("^\\[", path)) {
      stop(sprintf("BUG: path wrapped in array brackets: %s", path))
    }
    paste0("File written: ", path)
  },
  name = "write_file",
  description = "Write content to a file at the given path. Use RELATIVE paths only.",
  arguments = list(
    path = type_string("Relative file path to write to.", required = TRUE),
    content = type_string("The text content to write.", required = TRUE)
  )
)

read_file_tool <- tool(
  function(path) {
    cat("\n=== read_file CALLED ===\n")
    cat("  path value: ", repr::repr(path), "\n")
    if (grepl("^\\[", path)) {
      stop(sprintf("BUG: path wrapped in array brackets: %s", path))
    }
    "name: example\ndescription: An example skill."
  },
  name = "read_file",
  description = "Read a file at the given relative path.",
  arguments = list(
    path = type_string("Relative file path to read.", required = TRUE)
  )
)

walk_dir_tool <- tool(
  function(path) {
    cat("\n=== walk_directory CALLED ===\n")
    cat("  path value: ", repr::repr(path), "\n")
    '{"directories": ["scripts", "references"], "files": ["SKILL.md"]}'
  },
  name = "walk_directory",
  description = "List files and directories at the given relative path.",
  arguments = list(
    path = type_string(
      "Relative directory path. Use '.' for the root.",
      required = FALSE
    )
  )
)

chat$register_tool(write_file_tool)
chat$register_tool(read_file_tool)
chat$register_tool(walk_dir_tool)

# --- Trigger the bug with a multi-step prompt ---
cat("Sending request...\n\n")
#> Sending request...
result <- tryCatch(
  chat$chat(paste(
    "Create a skill directory structure with these files:",
    "1. First, list the current directory with (walk_directory())",
    "2. Write SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter (name: import-bids,",
    "   description: Import BIDS data into RAVE) and a markdown body (write_file())",
    "3. Write scripts/import-bids.R with a simple R script (write_file())",
    "4. Write references/parameters.md with parameter docs (write_file())",
    "5. List the directory again to confirm (walk_directory())"
  ), echo = "all"),
  error = function(e) {
    cat("\nERROR:", conditionMessage(e), "\n")
    traceback(e)
    e
  }
)
#> > Create a skill directory structure with these files: 1. First, list the 
#> > current directory with (walk_directory()) 2. Write SKILL.md with YAML 
#> > frontmatter (name: import-bids,    description: Import BIDS data into RAVE) 
#> > and a markdown body (write_file()) 3. Write scripts/import-bids.R with a 
#> > simple R script (write_file()) 4. Write references/parameters.md with 
#> > parameter docs (write_file()) 5. List the directory again to confirm 
#> > (walk_directory())
#> < I'll create a skill directory structure with the specified files. Let me 
#> < start by listing the current directory, then create the required files.
#> < 
#> < <function=walk_directory>
#> < <parameter=path>
#> < .
#> < </parameter>
#> < </function>
#> < </tool_call>
#> < [tool request (call_94hht6e6call_otldprbmcall_h0hdkdb8call_83nw84gd)]: 
#> < write_filewalk_directory()
#> [tool result  (call_94hht6e6call_otldprbmcall_h0hdkdb8call_83nw84gd)]: Error: Unknown tool
#> > [tool result  (call_94hht6e6call_otldprbmcall_h0hdkdb8call_83nw84gd)]: Error:
#> > Unknown tool
#> 
#> ERROR: HTTP 400 Bad Request.
#> ℹ invalid tool call arguments
#> Error in `x[[i]]`:
#> ! subscript out of bounds
```

description:
Hi, 

I'm trying to use Gemini through Google Vertex AI with service account credentials. According to the [documentation](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/reference/chat_google_gemini.html#authentication), ellmer should use Google's default application credentials if available, but in interactive mode it always triggers the browser-based OAuth flow instead.

title: Add models_groq()
description:
This is what we're using in metacheck:

```
#' Get Groq Models
#'
#' Returns a list of active models in groq. See <https://console.groq.com/docs/models> for more information.
#'
#' @returns a table of model info
#' @export
models_groq <- function() {
  API_KEY <- Sys.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY")
  url <- "https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models"
  config <- httr::add_headers(
    Authorization = paste("Bearer", API_KEY)
  )

  response <- httr::GET(
    url, config,
    encode = "json")

  models <- do.call(dplyr::bind_rows,
                    httr::content(response)$data) |>
    data.frame()

  # fix `created` column format to fit ellmer::models_platform() tables
  models$created_at <- as.POSIXct(models$created) |> format("%Y-%m-%d") |> as.Date()
  rows <- models$active
  cols <- names(models) |> setdiff(c("active", "created"))
  active <- models[rows, cols]

  return(active)
}
```

title: Feature Request: Implement Native "Agent" Class (ReAct Loop) for Autonomous Workflows
description:
he Problem: Lack of Autonomy
Currently, `ellmer` provides an excellent interface for one-shot or interactive chat. However, it lacks a native mechanism for autonomy.

To execute multi-step tasks (e.g., "Download this CSV, clean it, and plot the trend"), a user currently has to manually act as the "runtime"—copying code blocks, executing them, and pasting errors back into the chat. There is no persistent object capable of the ReAct (Reason + Act) pattern to handle this loop automatically.

 The Proposed Solution
I propose implementing a dedicated `Agent` class (likely an R6 object) that wraps the existing `Chat` interface to enable autonomous execution.

1. The `Agent` Class (The Brain)
A stateful object that manages a `while` loop of  Thought → Action → Observation.
* It would leverage the existing `chat` object for LLM calls.
* It would automatically handle context window management and recursion limits (`max_steps`).
* User Experience:
  ```r
  agent <- Agent$new(chat)
  agent$run("Analyze this dataset")

2. Strict Tool Interface Current tool definitions are flexible, but an Agent needs strict contracts. I propose a Tool class that:
* Wraps R functions (e.g., read.csv, ggplot).
* Automatically generates the JSON schema required by OpenAI/Anthropic (extracting params from formals()).
* Handles execution errors gracefully, feeding them back to the LLM for self-correction.

3. Safety & Sandboxing (Crucial) Autonomy requires safety. The Agent would include:
* File System Jail: Restricting I/O to a specific subdirectory (e.g., ./agent_scratchpad/).
* Human-in-the-Loop: A confirm_execution = TRUE mode where the user approves tools before they run.

Implementation Details
I have spent time analyzing ellmer's internals (specifically during my work on PR #906 regarding chat history architecture) and believe this can be implemented as a clean layer on top of the existing providers.

GSoC 2026 Participation
I have drafted a complete 5-page Technical Specification (including architecture diagrams and a 12-week timeline) for building this feature.

I would love to champion this implementation as a Google Summer of Code 2026 project.

Question for Maintainers: Is ellmer (or the Tidyverse team) considering participating in GSoC this year?

If so, I am ready to share the full proposal immediately. If not, I am still keen to discuss this design for future community contributions!

title: Problem using service json for Google authentication
get_token_cost() fails when API response lacks service_tier
description:
## Problem

I'm using ellmer with my company's internal OpenAI endpoint.

This worked in ellmer v0.3.0:

```r
library(ellmer)
chat <- chat_openai(
  model = "bedrock-anthropic-claude-3.7-sonnet",
  base_url = "internal-endpoint",
)
chat$chat("What is the difference between a tibble and a data frame?")
```

In ellmer v0.4.0, I'd start to get a response, then:

```
Error in data.frame(provider = provider@name, model = provider@model,
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 1, 0
```

## Likely Cause

`get_token_cost()` is called with `variant = NULL` when the API response doesn't include [`service_tier`](https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/blob/d26b150989eba931fa86ad46845a82f0bf54bb13/R/provider-openai.R#L326). The `data.frame()` call then fails because `variant` has length 0 while other columns have length 1.

## Potential Fix

Default variant to `NULL` and set to `""` if so:

```r
get_token_cost <- function(provider, tokens, variant = NULL) {
  variant <- variant %||% ""
  # ...
}
```

title: chat_github crashes on rate limit (429) due to invalid JSON body
description:
When using chat_github or other OpenAI-compatible providers and/or spamming with chat_parallel, hitting a rate limit (429 Too Many Requests) causes ellmer to crash with a JSON parsing error instead of retrying or reporting the error.

This occurs because the GitHub Models endpoint returns a Content-Type: application/json header but a plain text body "Too many requests... "etc. when rate limited... i.e. The base_request_error method attempts to parse this as JSON and fails.

Reproduction code
```
library(ellmer)
# Use a small model to hit rate limits quickly
chat <- chat_github(model = "gpt-4o-mini")
prompts <- as.list(paste("Say hello", 1:50))

# Trigger 429
tryCatch(
  parallel_chat(chat, prompts, max_active = 20),
  error = function(e) print(e)
) 
```

Proposed Fix- 
Update base_request_error in R/provider-openai-compatible.R to wrap resp_body_json() in a tryCatch. If JSON parsing fails, fall back to returning the raw string body. 
This allows httr2 to correctly identify the 429 error and apply retry logic.

I'll attempt a concise pull request...

title: Clarify how to set temperature with chat_ollama(). It isn't  obvious it goes in api_args
description:
@hadley — first off, **ellmer** is fantastic package, and has become my daily driver for local LLMs in R. Thank you!

I ran into a small documentation gotcha that I think many users might hit. That,  it isn't  immediately obvious  with chat_ollama() you have to set temperature (and other Ollama options) via the api_args list, rather than as top-level arguments.

The generic chat() function exposes .temperature directly, but chat_ollama() routes everything through api_args. Temperature is one of the most commonly tweaked parameters in production LLM use. People routinely set it low (0.0–0.3) for deterministic, reproducible outputs in applications like trading signals, automated reporting, legal summaries, or any situation where the same prompt should give the same answer every time. Without clear documentation, users waste time trying .temperature = 0.2 at the top level, as I did (which throws “unused argument”) or in chat$chat(). A one-line example in ?chat_ollama or the vignette would save a lot of head-scratching.

```
chat <- chat_ollama(
  model = "qwen2.5:7b",
  api_args = list(temperature = 0.2)   # low randomness → consistent verdicts
)

```

title: intermittent failures tool calling with OpenRouter
description:
On OpenRouter, even models like Claude Sonnet seem to have trouble consistently passing arguments that are compliant with the tool description. Performance of models seems to degrade on OpenRouter compared to the usual provider (in this case, Anthropic, but I observed this with many other model families). I also tested setting the provider within OpenRouter to the same API that the native provider ultimately hits, and still saw that degradation. So, I think there's an actual issue with the implementation of `chat_openrouter()`.

It appears that, when conversation history is sent back to OpenRouter, `jsonlite::toJSON()` serializes tool call arguments without `auto_unbox = TRUE`, wrapping scalar values in arrays, e.g. `"path":["R/file.R"]` instead of `"path":"R/file.R"`. The model sees this format and intermittently mimics it in subsequent responses, producing malformed arguments like `"[\"file\"]"`.

Here's a reprex--I had hoped to make it more minimal, but it seems to require two different, relatively complex tools, called in sequence. Even then, this only failed after 5 successes. (Note that it needs to be ran with `wd = "."`.) Note the `limit = "[100]", case_sensitive = "[false]"` rather than `"100"` and `FALSE`.

library(ellmer)

# for an example tool that has some non-trivial arguments
library(btw)

client <- chat_openrouter(model = "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5")
client$set_system_prompt("Be very terse.")
client$register_tool(btw_tool_files_list_files)
client$register_tool(btw_tool_files_code_search)

title: chat_github() fails with 404 (API not supported) and models_github() errors in v0.4.0
description:
In ellmer 0.4.0, chat_github() fails to connect to both the default GitHub Models endpoint (models.github.ai) and the Azure endpoint (models.inference.ai.azure.com).
The Problem

chat_github(): This function wraps chat_openai(). In v0.4.0, chat_openai() defaults to the experimental /responses endpoint and includes parameters like service_tier and store. The GitHub/Azure endpoints do not support this path or these parameters, resulting in a 404 Not Found or "API not supported" error.
models_github(): Fails with attempt to apply non-function. It appears the base_url is not being passed correctly to the ProviderOpenAI constructor.

Reproduction

```
library(ellmer)

# 1. Fails with 404 (API not supported)
chat <- chat_github(model = "gpt-4o")
chat$chat("ping") 

# 2. Fails with "attempt to apply non-function"
ellmer::models_github() 
```

workaround

Manual testing via httr2 confirms that both endpoints work correctly when using the standard /chat/completions path without extra OpenAI parameters.

Using chat_openai_compatible (which uses the standard path) works immediately:

```
  # This works:
  chat <- chat_openai_compatible(
    base_url = "https://models.github.ai/inference", 
    model = "gpt-4o",
    credentials = function() list(Authorization = paste("Bearer", Sys.getenv("GITHUB_PAT")))
  )
chat$chat("ping")
```

Suggested Fix

chat_github() should likely wrap chat_openai_compatible() instead of chat_openai() to ensure it uses the standard /chat/completions endpoint supported by GitHub Models.
