title: chat_openai()` adds `service_tier` parameter causing incompatibility with OpenAI-compatible APIs (litellm, etc.)
description:
## Summary

`chat_openai()` automatically adds a `service_tier` parameter to API requests, which causes errors when connecting to OpenAI-compatible APIs that don't support this parameter (e.g., litellm proxy, local OpenAI servers).

## Environment

- **ellmer version**: Latest (as of 2024-11-20)
- **R version**: 4.x
- **API**: OpenAI-compatible API using litellm as proxy

## Problem Description

### Symptom

When using `chat_openai()` with an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint (in our case, an internal API using litellm as a proxy to Azure OpenAI):

```r
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_openai(
  system_prompt = "You are an expert R programmer",
  model = "claude-4-sonnet",
  base_url = "https://our-internal-api.example.com/v1",
  api_key = Sys.getenv("API_KEY")
)

response <- chat$chat("Generate R code...")
```

**Error received:**
```
HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
litellm.APIConnectionError: litellm.main.acompletion() got multiple values 
for keyword argument 'service_tier'
```

### Root Cause

1. **`chat_openai()` automatically adds `service_tier` parameter**
   - This parameter is specific to the official OpenAI API
   - It's used to select processing priority: "auto" or "default"
   - Added automatically in the HTTP POST request body

2. **OpenAI-compatible APIs may not support `service_tier`**
   - litellm (a popular LLM proxy) doesn't recognize this parameter
   - Local OpenAI servers may not implement it
   - Other OpenAI-compatible APIs may reject it

3. **HTTP Request generated by `chat_openai()`:**

```http
POST https://our-internal-api.example.com/v1/chat/completions
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <api_key>

{
  "model": "claude-4-sonnet",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are an expert R programmer"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Generate R code..."}
  ],
  "service_tier": "auto",  ← PROBLEM: Not supported by all APIs
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "max_tokens": 4000
}
```

## Current Workaround

We discovered that `chat_openai_compatible()` **does not** add the `service_tier` parameter, making it work perfectly with OpenAI-compatible APIs:

```r
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_openai_compatible(
  system_prompt = "You are an expert R programmer",
  base_url = "https://our-internal-api.example.com/v1",
  api_key = Sys.getenv("API_KEY"),
  model = "claude-4-sonnet"
)

response <- chat$chat("Generate R code...")
# ✅ Works perfectly!
```

### Our Solution: Wrapper Functions

We created wrapper functions to simplify usage:

```r
# Wrapper that reads environment variables automatically
chat_custom_api <- function(
  system_prompt = NULL,
  model = "claude-4-sonnet",
  params = NULL,
  echo = c("none", "output", "all")
) {
  
  api_url <- Sys.getenv("CUSTOM_API_URL")
  api_key <- Sys.getenv("CUSTOM_API_KEY")
  
  if (api_url == "" || api_key == "") {
    stop("Environment variables CUSTOM_API_URL and CUSTOM_API_KEY required")
  }
  
  # Use chat_openai_compatible() instead of chat_openai()
  ellmer::chat_openai_compatible(
    system_prompt = system_prompt,
    base_url = api_url,
    api_key = api_key,
    model = model,
    params = params,
    echo = echo
  )
}

# Usage
chat <- chat_custom_api(
  system_prompt = "You are an expert R programmer"
)
```

## Comparison

| Aspect | `chat_openai()` | `chat_openai_compatible()` |
|--------|-----------------|----------------------------|
| **Adds `service_tier`** | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
| **Works with official OpenAI API** | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes |
| **Works with litellm** | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
| **Works with local OpenAI servers** | ❌ Maybe not | ✅ Yes |
| **Works with other compatible APIs** | ❌ Maybe not | ✅ Yes |

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Make `service_tier` optional in `chat_openai()`

Add a parameter to disable `service_tier`:

```r
chat_openai <- function(
  ...,
  service_tier = "auto",  # or NULL to disable
  ...
) {
  # Only add service_tier if not NULL
  if (!is.null(service_tier)) {
    body$service_tier <- service_tier
  }
}
```

### Option 2: Document the difference between `chat_openai()` and `chat_openai_compatible()`

Clarify in the documentation that:
- `chat_openai()` is for the official OpenAI API (includes OpenAI-specific parameters)
- `chat_openai_compatible()` is for OpenAI-compatible APIs (minimal parameter set)

### Option 3: Auto-detect API compatibility

Try to detect if the API supports `service_tier` and adjust accordingly (though this might be complex).

## Impact

This issue affects users who want to:
- Connect to local OpenAI-compatible servers
- Use litellm as a proxy
- Connect to internal/corporate OpenAI-compatible APIs
- Use alternative LLM providers with OpenAI-compatible endpoints

## Additional Context

- **Why `service_tier` exists**: It's an OpenAI-specific feature for request prioritization
- **Why it fails with litellm**: litellm is a unified proxy for multiple LLM providers and doesn't implement all OpenAI-specific features
- **Our use case**: Internal corporate API using Azure OpenAI + litellm proxy

## Workaround Summary

For now, users experiencing this issue should use `chat_openai_compatible()` instead of `chat_openai()` when connecting to OpenAI-compatible APIs.

## Related

- OpenAI API documentation on `service_tier`: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/create#chat-create-service_tier
- litellm documentation: https://docs.litellm.ai/

---

**Thank you for the excellent ellmer package!** This is a minor compatibility issue, but documenting it would help users connecting to OpenAI-compatible APIs.

title: chat_structured() silently fails when response hits max_tokens limit
description:
When `chat_structured()` exceeds `max_tokens`, it returns empty/incorrect values with no warning or error. I ran into this trying to extract large bibliographies from scientific articles using claude-sonnet-4-5 with the default output size of 4096 tokens. The whole output schema was NULL. A warning to bump up output context size using params would help users understand what's going on here!

## Reproducible Example

Created with `reprex::reprex(session_info = TRUE)`:

```r
library(ellmer)

# Schema with array field
schema <- ellmer::type_object(
  sentences = ellmer::type_array(
    items = ellmer::type_string(),
    description = "Array of all sentences"
  )
)

# Use low max_tokens to force truncation
chat <- ellmer::chat(
  name = "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5",
  system_prompt = "You are a helpful assistant.",
  params = list(max_tokens = 100)
)

large_context <- paste(rep("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet. ", 500), collapse = "")
result <- chat$chat_structured(large_context, type = schema)

# Check response
turns <- chat$get_turns()
last_turn <- turns[[length(turns)]]

last_turn@json$stop_reason         # "max_tokens"
last_turn@json$usage$output_tokens # 100
class(result$sentences)            # "character" (should be "list")
result$sentences                   # "" (empty string)
```

<sup>Created on YYYY-MM-DD with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

<details style="margin-bottom:10px;"><summary>Session info</summary>

```
─ Session info ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 setting  value
 version  R version 4.4.x
 os       macOS
 system   x86_64, darwin
 ellmer   0.3.2
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```

</details>

## Observed Behavior

1. API returns `stop_reason: "max_tokens"`
2. Tool input is empty: `{}`
3. `chat_structured()` returns result with empty/default values
4. No warning or error is raised
5. Type mismatch: array field returns as character instead of list

## Expected Behavior

When `stop_reason == "max_tokens"`:

1. Throw error: "Response exceeded max_tokens limit. Increase max_tokens or simplify schema."
2. OR return partial results with warning
3. OR attempt to repair truncated JSON and return partial results

```r
reprex::reprex(session_info = TRUE)
#> ℹ Non-interactive session, setting `html_preview = FALSE`.
#> CLIPR_ALLOW has not been set, so clipr will not run interactively
```

title: Clarify possible return values from tool
description:
Tools can return strings, complex objects (converted to JSON), JSON, and, as of #735, `Content`s and lists of `Content`s. But it's hard to see that from `invoke_tool()` since the coercion doesn't happen until much later in `tool_string()`. I suggest that we create and store the JSON at invoke time, radically simplifying `tool_string()`. We can then verify the tool has returned the expected value, throwing an error to R (not the model, I think) indicating what's wrong.

To make errors more obvious, I'd suggest we also stop automatically converting complex objects to JSON, instead deprecating that behaviour and relying on the user to be explicit about it. Then we can say something like: A tool must return a string, an atomic vector, JSON, `Content`,  or a list of `Content`s.

(Extracted from https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/pull/735#discussion_r2519922179 and https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/pull/735#discussion_r2520109343)

title: chat_groq() returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized despite valid API key (dev v0.4.0+)
description:
### Problem
`chat_groq()` for ellmer Version: 0.3.2.9000 fails with 401 Unauthorized ("Invalid API Key") on basic chat, even with explicit `credentials` function providing a valid Groq key. Raw `httr` requests to the same endpoint/models succeed. Non-streaming and streaming both fail at the auth step. library(ellmer)

  list(api_key = Sys.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY"))
}

chat <- chat_groq(
  model = "llama-3.1-8b-instant",
  credentials = groq_creds  # Or api_key = Sys.getenv("GROQ_API_KEY") for older

title: Error handling clarification for batch requests
description:
I've been experimenting with `batch_chat_structured` using OpenAI models, and while I noted that the documentation calls out its experimental nature, specifically with regards to error handling, I would appreciate some clarification about what exactly _is_ happening when errors are encountered.

A fairly common experience for me so far (~50% of batch jobs I've run), OpenAI's web UI for batches will report, e.g. `Request counts
1000 completed, 0 failed of 1000 total requests`. But even so, both an output file _and_ an error file will be generated with a handful of input prompts listed in the error file. So the output file available for download in the web UI may have 990 lines and the error file will have 10. Typically, the information in the error file is not terribly informative, e.g.

```
{"id": "batch_req_690a0b6dbf608190b85f266e675c42a4", "custom_id": "chat-186", "response": {"status_code": 0, "request_id": "", "body": {}}, "error": null}
```

Rarely, the status code will be a recognizable http error code like 500 or 503, but almost always it is just 0.

If I fetch the results from R by re-running `batch_chat_structured` I get a warning from `mapply`:

```
Warning in mapply(.f, .x, .y, MoreArgs = list(...), SIMPLIFY = FALSE) :
  longer argument not a multiple of length of shorter
```

but the resulting data frame has the same number of rows as my input prompts. Even more confusingly (for me), if the error file lists `chat-186` and that chat item is missing from the output file, the 186th row of the data frame generated in R by re-running `batch_chat_structured` _does_ have data in it. 

Given all this I'm confused about how ellmer is generating a full set of results and whether they are in the same order as the input prompts.

Any additional information on what precisely is happening in these circumstances would be greatly appreciated!

Edit: On other similar occasions, re-running `batch_chat_structured` fails completely with an uninformative parse error:

```
Error: parse error: premature EOF
                                       
                     (right here) ------^
```

In those cases, manually downloading both the output & error files from the web UI, they are both successfully parsed by `jsonlite::stream_in`, so I'm confused where ellmer is having parsing difficulties.

Edit: Ah, it seems the premature EOF happens when the LLM fails at its job and instead of structured json returns only `""` in the `content` portion of `message`. I suppose it would be nice if ellmer could handle a few degenerate failure modes there, although I realize you can't anticipate every possible malformed output from the LLM.

title: Figure out `chat_openai_compatible()` strategy
description:
From https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/pull/635#discussion_r2448459119

> My 2¢ is that `chat_openai()` is too useful of a function for users to deprecate. I think most users will want to just call `chat_openai()` to start talking to OpenAI models and they won't care at all about the difference in the underlying API.
> 
> Personally, I think it's reasonable to push the messiness of the abstractions into the Provider layers, so I really like `ProviderOpenAIResponses` and an alternate named `ProviderOpenAICompletions` or `ProviderOpenAIApi` or `ProviderOpenAICompatible` (leaning toward the first).
> 
> The problem is that there are likely many uses of `chat_openai()` that currently target the `completions` endpoint and are taking advantage of an API marketed as "OpenAI-compatible". If it's possible to catch those use-cases at runtime — e.g. by looking for an error message that would occur if `chat_openai()` tries to use the responses endpoint on a server that doesn't support it — then ellmer could provide migration instructions and point people to a new `chat_openai_compatible()` or `chat_openai_api()` that uses the alternate provider.
> 
> I suppose that if it's not possible to provide run-time migration advice, my opinion about the `chat_openai()` name _might_ change. From an educational perspective, I would much rather teach people to use `chat_openai()` to talk to OpenAI models than to have to teach `chat_openai_responses()` just to get started. That name is more appropriate for users who are using "off-label" `chat_openai()`, and those more advanced users are also aware of the fast-moving nature of this space. In general, I think everyone will understand the need for breaking changes in this area, especially if those changes protect the getting started and most common user experiences.

```
library(ellmer)

chat_direct <- ellmer::chat_aws_bedrock(
  model = "anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0"
)

chat_direct$chat("Please tell me a joke about R programmers")

#But using an application inference profile errors out
chat_application_profile <- ellmer::chat_aws_bedrock(
  model = "arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:<redacted_aws_account_number>:application-inference-profile/<redacted_inference_profile>")
  
chat_application_profile$chat("Please tell me a joke about R programmers")
```
The application profile chat returns the following error:
```
Error: <ellmer::Turn> object properties are invalid:
- @json must be <list>, not <NULL>
In addition: Warning message:
Premature end of input; ignoring final partial chunk 
Error during wrapup: cannot get a slot ("slots") from an object of type "NULL"
Error: no more error handlers available (recursive errors?); invoking 'abort' restart

```
If we use the `chat_async` method instead of `chat` we no longer get an error, but still don't get a response

```
#chat_async method still works with direct model access
chat_direct <- ellmer::chat_aws_bedrock(
  model = "anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20240620-v1:0"
)
chat_direct$chat_async("Please tell me a joke about R programmers")

print(chat_direct)

# with application inference profile we no longer get an error, but the response is empty
chat_application_profile <- ellmer::chat_aws_bedrock(
  model = "arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:<redacted_aws_account_number>:application-inference-profile/<redacted_inference_profile>"
)

chat_application_profile$chat_async("Please tell me a joke about R programmers")

print(chat_application_profile)
```
This print statement returns:
```
<Chat AWS/Bedrock/arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:<redacted_aws_account_number>:application-inference-profile/<redacted_inference_profile> turns=2 tokens=0/0>
── user [0]────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Please tell me a joke about R programmers
── assistant [0]──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

```

Using paws::bedrockruntime directly the application inference profile works fine:
```
bedrock <- paws::bedrockruntime(config = list(region = "us-east-1"))

response <- bedrock$converse(
  modelId = "arn:aws:bedrock:us-east-1:<redacted_aws_account_number>:application-inference-profile/<redacted_inference_profile>",
  messages = list(
    list(
      role = "user",
      content = list(
        list(text = "Please tell me a joke about R programmers")

)
```

title: support images in tool call output with OpenAI
description:
This is a revival of #617.

In the [docs for the completions API](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat?api-mode=chat), the link to function calling heads to [this page](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling#:~:text=Tool%20call%20outputs%20%2D%20output%20we%20generate%20for%20the%20model). Under "Tool call outputs - output we generate for the model", I see:

> "The **tool call output** might return a JSON object (e.g., `{"temperature": "25", "unit": "C"}`, indicating a current temperature of 25 degrees), [Image contents](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/images), or [File contents](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/pdf-files)."

That linked "Image contents" page is just the docs for the [usual entry point](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/images-vision?api-mode=chat&format=base64-encoded#giving-a-model-images-as-input) from that used in user chat input.

I decided to give a go at using the same interface while working on an eval today, and am seeing convincing results; only counted as ~1000 tokens and reasonably strong visual understanding.

title: Chats forget about structured data
description:
In my use case, I need to refine and iterate on an AI-generated structured dataset over the course of a long conversation. But in a chat, downstream replies seem oblivious to any structured data previously generated. What is the best way to make the LLM remember what it outputs?

Here's a reprex:

``` r
library(ellmer)
chat <- chat_anthropic()
#> Using model = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514".
chat$chat_structured(
  "Generate the name and age of a random person.",
  type = type_object(
    name = type_string(),
    age = type_number()
  )
)
#> $name
#> [1] "Sarah Mitchell"
#> 
#> $age
#> [1] 34
chat$chat("What was the name and age you just generated?")
#> I actually didn't generate a specific name and age in my previous response. I 
#> can see that my response just showed "<structured data/>" which appears to be a
#> formatting artifact, but didn't contain any actual name or age.
#>

chat$chat("But what was the first prompt I gave you?")
#> Your first prompt was: "Generate the name and age of a random person."
```

title: Allow for multiple output
description:
Hi,

Thank you for developing these excellent packages. As a beginner with ellmer and shinychat, I'm interested in learning how to return multiple outputs in a single chat round via tool calling.

In R/Shiny, returning a list (e.g., `return(list(A = fig1, B = fig2, C = data.frame(), D = Text))`) is the typical approach. Is it possible for ellmer's `Content()` function to bundle multiple output types in one response, like:
```
Content(
  ContentImage(fig1),
  ContentImage(fig2),
  ContentTable(my_table),
  ContentText(glue::glue('My summary text here'))
)
```

In my use case, my tool calling function needs to output and shinychatbox should display:
1. Two figures (ggplot objects)
2. One table (e.g., a gt HTML table)
3. One character sentence (e.g., using glue with variables)

I haven't been able to find documentation or tutorials covering this multi-output approach in ellmer/shinychat. I did read your post at https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/pull/735, but that covers only figures. 

I also saw a shinychat article covering `ContentToolResults()` (https://posit-dev.github.io/shinychat/r/articles/tool-ui.html#alternative-display-content), but it seems to only allow a sentence and table via an extra argument, rather than arbitrary outputs.

Please let me know if this question would be better suited for Stack Overflow.

Thank you for any guidance!

title: Shim `system.file()` in `interpolate_package()` to support local development
description:
_Originally posted by @gadenbuie in https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/pull/763#discussion_r2394887696_

One bit of friction with `interpolate_package()` is that `pkgload` shims `system.file()` in the global env and in the loaded package namespace, so `interpolate_package()` doesn't work with dev packages.

Where I've needed that, I've written an internal `interpolate_package()` that replicated ellmer's implementation. But it'd be nice if there were a way around this. (The Shiny team has a `system_file()` function in [Winston's staticimports package](https://github.com/wch/staticimports/blob/35ceec8d9d9429d9244aedc3ee6a1e8d62d59f79/inst/staticexports/package.R#L35-L41), but maybe there's rlang helper I haven't encountered yet?)

@hadley wrote:

> Yeah, I think it's probably worth testing if package is a dev package (i.e. implement the shim ourselves).

title: use of short and long-term API keys with AWS Bedrock
description:
I am looking for a potential way to use API keys with ellmer and the AWS bedrock implementation. I have been able to connect up and use the chat object with AWS via the PAWS integration and SSO, but have been unable to find documentation on how one might use this package with API keys instead of SSO authentication.

The AWS bedrock documentation does provide a way to use API keys using their boto3 package: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys-use.html

```
import os
import boto3
                        
# If you already set the API key as an environment variable, you can comment this line out                        
os.environ['AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK'] = "${api-key}"

# Create an Amazon Bedrock client
client = boto3.client(
    service_name="bedrock-runtime",
    region_name="us-east-1" # If you've configured a default region, you can omit this line
)

# Define the model and message
model_id = "us.anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0"
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Hello"}]}]

response = client.converse(
    modelId=model_id,
    messages=messages,
)
```

They also have some documentation about using an API key in the header request of an HTTP API request.

I have been unable to find documentation on how to make this happen in Ellmer despite trying to create key value pairs for the api key as `params()` in a custom chat object. Is there a way? Please help if able. Thank you!

title: `chat()` ends up with a different default value for `echo` than direct chat functions
description:
```r
library(ellmer)

chat("openai")$chat("Hi there") # doesn't stream (echo="none")
```

title: AWS Bedrock provider intermittently creates duplicate ContentJson objects, causing extraction failures
description:
## Problem Summary

The AWS Bedrock provider sometimes creates duplicate ContentJson objects from a single model response, causing `extract_data()` to fail with "Data extraction failed: 2 data results received."

## Environment
   
- **Provider:** AWS Bedrock (`chat_aws_bedrock`)
- **Model:** `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0` (likely affects other Bedrock models)
- **Function:** `parallel_chat_structured()` and `chat_structured()`

## Expected Behavior

`extract_data()` should receive exactly 1 ContentJson object per structured response.

## Actual Behavior

Intermittently (non-deterministically), `extract_data()` receives 2 identical ContentJson objects from the same response, causing extraction to fail.

## Reproduction

The issue is intermittent but can be reproduced by running structured extraction multiple times. I will post a repress of the error below. But generically,

  ```r
  # Setup
  chat <- chat_aws_bedrock(
    model = "us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0",
    system_prompt = "Extract structured data...",
    api_args = list(inferenceConfig = list(seed = 26082025, temperature = 0))
  )

  # Run multiple times - failures occur randomly
  for (i in 1:10) {
    tryCatch({
      result <- chat$chat_structured(some_text, type = some_type)
    }, error = function(e) {
      if (grepl("2 data results", e$message)) {
        cat("Failure on attempt", i, "\n")
      }
    })
  }
```

##  Investigation Results

-  All failure cases show exactly 2 identical ContentJson objects (not different responses)
-  Success cases show exactly 1 ContentJson object
-  The issue appears to be in the Bedrock provider's response parsing, not the model output
-  Non-deterministic despite fixed seed, suggesting a parsing race condition or API state issue

##  Impact

-  Causes `parallel_chat_structured()` batch jobs to fail partway through

##  Proposed Solution

Modify `extract_data()` to handle duplicate ContentJson objects by:
1. Detecting when n=2 JSON objects are identical
2. Using the first object and issuing a warning
3. Still failing if JSON objects are genuinely different (unexpected case)

title: New Feature Request : Support Microsoft POML (Prompt Orchestration Markup Language) in ellmer
description: Hi Team, Source : https://microsoft.github.io/poml/latest/ ``` POML (Prompt Orchestration Markup Language) is a novel markup language designed to bring structure, maintainability, and versatility to advanced prompt engineering for Large Language Models (LLMs). It addresses common challenges in prompt development, such as lack of structure, complex data integration, format sensitivity, and inadequate tooling. POML provides a systematic way to organize prompt components, integrate diverse data types seamlessly, and manage presentation variations, empowering developers to create more sophisticated and reliable LLM applications. Key Features[¶](https://microsoft.github.io/poml/latest/#key-features) Structured Prompting Markup: Employs an HTML-like syntax with semantic components such as , , and to encourage modular design, enhancing prompt readability, reusability, and maintainability. Comprehensive Data Handling: Incorporates specialized data components (e.g., , , ) that seamlessly embed or reference external data sources like text files, spreadsheets, and images, with customizable formatting options. Decoupled Presentation Styling: Features a CSS-like styling system that separates content from presentation. This allows developers to modify styling (e.g., verbosity, syntax format) via definitions or inline attributes without altering core prompt logic, mitigating LLM format sensitivity. Integrated Templating Engine: Includes a built-in templating engine with support for variables ({{ }}), loops (for), conditionals (if), and variable definitions () for dynamically generating complex, data-driven prompts. ``` Thanks Arun

title: parsers for chat responses?
description:
Would it be in-scope to provide parsers to extract elements of the response?  

For instance, many models will reply with various use of markdown, JSON, and XML syntax, like:

```
<think>
species classification blah blah...
<think>

I found the following classification:

{"kingdom": "Animalia", "phylum": "Chordata"}

```

We might want to pull out the different parts of this reply and handle them differently (e.g. hide/suppress `think` tag bit, parse the JSON, separately isolate the plain-text explanation.  

(Another common pattern beyond the one above is the use of markdown code chunks, where we might want to parse out the literal code and possibly a language indicator, if present).  

I see we now have the experimental [formatters](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org/reference/contents_text.html) to adjust visual display of the response, which is awesome, but I think this would be the complementary side.  

Obviously we can just go at it with regex etc but feels pretty clunky.  We can also use the system prompt to try and convince the LLM to only reply in JSON, say, but it will still sometimes add xml tags (like with the think / reasoning models -- at least Qwen reasoning models do this)

 Or maybe there's already a better way to be approaching this?  Apologies if this already exists and I haven't looked in the right place!

title: Streaming breaks with OpenAI-compatible APIs that omit usage data
description:
## Problem
I'm using ellmer within my company (Boehringer Ingelheim). We have an OpenAI-compatible API service called Apollo. The output of Apollo's chat.completion when `stream = TRUE` doesn't include `usage` information in the streaming chunks. This causes ellmer to crash during token logging. 

I've found that the error happens in `tokens_row()` when ellmer tries to create a data frame. Some fields have data but the usage fields are NULL, so you get mismatched row counts. Specifically, it throws this error: `Error in data.frame: arguments imply differing number of rows: 1, 0`. 

Here's what a chat completion chunk looks like from Apollo when streaming (omitting the non-relevant parts):
```json
{
  "choices": [{"delta": {"content": "Hello"}}],
  "usage": null
}
```

Compare this to OpenAI which sends usage data in the final chunk (this is also what our Apollo service looks like when giving non-streaming responses):
```json
{
  "choices": [{"delta": {"content": ""}}],
  "usage": {"completion_tokens": 5, "prompt_tokens": 10, ...}
}
```

## Steps to reproduce
Unfortunately, I can't give you a Boehringer Ingelheim account for you to test this with, so you're just gonna have to trust me :)

## Expected behavior
This shouldn't break streaming. Either skip token logging when usage is missing, or use 0/NA as defaults.

## Impact
This makes ellmer incompatible with our internal OpenAI-compatible service. The streaming content works fine - it's just the token logging that fails at the end.

Currently I have to catch this error and fall back to non-streaming mode, which defeats the purpose of streaming, and makes the usage of ellmer burdensome for users, especially when using tool calls and the wait time becomes longer. 

## Problematic code

I believe the issue occurs in `/R/provider-openai.R` at lines 272-277 in the `value_turn()` method:

```r
cached_tokens <- result$usage$prompt_tokens_details$cached_tokens %||% 0
tokens <- tokens_log(
  provider,
  input = result$usage$prompt_tokens - cached_tokens,
  output = result$usage$completion_tokens,
  cached_input = cached_tokens
)
```

When `result$usage` is `NULL` (as with Apollo), attempting to access `result$usage$prompt_tokens` throws an error **before** the null-coalescing operator `%||%` and the existing null handling in `tokens_log()` can take effect.

## Solution

I'm more than happy to submit the PR here, because I think I've found a good solution and its pretty easy to implement (at least for when the provider is "OpenAI"):

```r
if (is.null(result$usage)) {
  tokens <- tokens_log(provider, input = NULL, output = NULL, cached_input = NULL)
} else {
  cached_tokens <- result$usage$prompt_tokens_details$cached_tokens %||% 0
  tokens <- tokens_log(
    provider,
    input = result$usage$prompt_tokens - cached_tokens,
    output = result$usage$completion_tokens,
    cached_input = cached_tokens
  )
}
```

When testing this, the symptoms I mentioned above go away, and I can happily use streaming w/ {ellmer} + Apollo. 

The proposed fix would make the OpenAI provider more robust and consistent with how usage should be handled when it's missing from API responses. Not sure if there are any knock-on effects of this change, however. I imagine it would impact the token usage and cost reporting functionality, but since our service doesn't even provide token usage there's no way we can use it anyway.

title: Api key and system prompt are lost when passing a chat object to a mirai/purrr::in_parallel worker
description:
Hello!

Just a heads up.

After much headache, I discovered that if you pass/clone a chat object into a Mirai worker, it loses certain information, for example the API key and the system prompt:

```r
# Build chat object, key is taken from the env
chat_base <- ellmer::chat_openrouter(model = "qwen/qwen3-coder:free")

mirai::mirai_map(
    1,
    function(i) {
        # show what the worker sees
        cat("Worker", i, "api key:", chat$get_provider()@api_key, "\n")
        chat$chat("Hello")            # fails if key missing
    },
    chat = chat_base
)[]
```
>[[1]]
>'miraiError' chr Error in req_auth_bearer_token(req, provider@api_key): `token` must be a single string, not `NULL`.

The only ways I found to obviate this is either to reconstruct the chat inside the work, or, even one already has to deal with a chat object as in my case, pass the provider + the lost info:

```r
mirai::mirai_map(
    1,
    function(i) {
        
        provider@api_key <- api_key
        
        chat_new <- ellmer:::Chat$new(
            provider = provider,
            system_prompt = system_prompt,
            echo = "none"
        )
        
        chat_new$chat("hi")
    },
    provider = chat_base$get_provider(),
    system_prompt = "this is a test",
    api_key = chat_base$get_provider()@api_key
)[]
```
>[[1]]
>Hello! How can I help you today?

Is this by design?

A label is a key-value pair that you can assign to generateContent and streamGenerateContent API calls. They help you organize these calls and manage your costs at scale, with the granularity you need. You can attach a label to each call, then filter the calls based on their labels. Information about labels is forwarded to the billing system that lets you break down your billed charges by label. With built-in [billing reports](https://cloud.google.com/billing/docs/how-to/reports), you can filter and group costs by labels.

Common use cases for labels
Team or cost center labels: Add labels based on team or cost center to distinguish API calls owned by different teams (for example, team:research and team:analytics). You can use this type of label for cost accounting or budgeting.
Component labels: For example, component:redis, component:frontend, component:ingest, and component:dashboard.
Environment or stage labels: For example, environment:production and environment:test.
Ownership labels: Used to identify the teams that are responsible for operations, for example: team:shopping-cart.

R Code to access via REST API

```R
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)

# ---- STEP 1: Set your values ----
project_id <- "your-project-id"            # <-- Replace with your GCP project ID
location <- "us-central1"                  # <-- Replace with region (e.g., us-central1)
model_id <- "gemini-1.5-pro-preview-0409"  # <-- Replace with your model ID
response_method <- "generateContent"       # or "streamGenerateContent"

# Prompt and labels
prompt_text <- "What are the key benefits of using generative AI in financial services?"
label_key <- "env"
label_value <- "test"

# ---- STEP 2: Get access token from gcloud ----
access_token <- system("gcloud auth print-access-token", intern = TRUE)

# ---- STEP 3: Prepare request body ----
body <- list(
  contents = list(
    role = "USER",
    parts = list(text = prompt_text)
  ),
  labels = setNames(list(label_value), label_key)
)

# ---- STEP 4: Convert to JSON ----
json_body <- toJSON(body, auto_unbox = TRUE)

# ---- STEP 5: Make POST request ----
url <- sprintf("https://%s-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/%s/locations/%s/publishers/google/models/%s:%s",
               location, project_id, location, model_id, response_method)

res <- POST(
  url,
  add_headers(
    Authorization = paste("Bearer", access_token),
    `Content-Type` = "application/json; charset=utf-8"
  ),
  body = json_body
)

# ---- STEP 6: View the response ----
cat(content(res, "text", encoding = "UTF-8"))
```

I can't really tell where the extra `"content_list": [...]` part of the request body is coming from because I'm not really familiar with the S7 object oriented stuff going on in `provider-snowflake.R`, but I think that's the issue.

title: Injection in tool function happens when creating a `tool()`
description:
I haven't investigated this deeply and I'm not sure if there's anything we can do about this. It seems that injection operators – like `!!var` and `{{ var }}` – are evaluated eagerly when a tool function is defined inline.

``` r
pkgload::load_all()
#> ℹ Loading ellmer

tool(
  function(cyl) {
    dplyr::filter(mtcars, cyl == !!cyl)
  },
  name = "filter_cyl",
  description = "Filter mtcars by number of cylinders",
  arguments = list(
    cyl = type_number("Number of cylinders")
  )
)
#> Error: object 'cyl' not found
```

The way around this is to define the function first and pass it to `tool()`.

```r
filter_cyl <- function(cyl) {
  dplyr::filter(mtcars, cyl == !!cyl)
}

tool(
  filter_cyl,
  description = "Filter mtcars by number of cylinders",
  arguments = list(
    cyl = type_number("Number of cylinders")
  )
)
#> # <ellmer::ToolDef> filter_cyl(cyl)
#> # @name: filter_cyl
#> # @description: Filter mtcars by number of cylinders
#> # @convert: TRUE
#> #
#> function (cyl) 
#> {
#>     dplyr::filter(mtcars, cyl == !!cyl)
#> }
```

I **love** the functionality of returning a data.frame from `parallel_chat_structured()` especially when `include_tokens = FALSE,
  include_cost = FALSE`. However: My use case crashes on the df conversion and then all of the results are lost. When `convert = FALSE`, there is no crash, and I can convert the result myself (but the tokens and cost info is lost).

Example is the R version (we did the original in Python, it was before **ellmer** could do this) of the analysis from Benoit, Kenneth, Scott De Marchi, Conor Laver, Michael Laver, and Jinshuai Ma. (in press) "[Using Large Language Models to Analyze Political Texts Through Natural Language Understanding](https://kenbenoit.net/pdfs/Benoit_etal_2025_AJPS.pdf)." _American Journal of Political Science_.

``` r
You will score the text on two dimensions of party policy: economic, and social liberalism.

After reading the manifesto, respond with the following information:

The name of the party who has written the manifesto [Party_LLM]; the name of the country where the party exists [Country_LLM]; the language in which the manifesto was written [Language_LLM]; a numerical score for the specific policy dimension as defined for each dimension ranging from 1 to 7 [score], followed by a brief justification for the score in English (regardless of the natural language of the original input text), citing specific language or themes from the text [evidence].

Do not output any additional text or commentary beyond the Party_LLM, Country_LLM, dimension, score and evidence.

-----

Dimension: Economic

For the following text of a party manifesto, please classify the party position on the tradeoff between higher spending on public services and lower taxation, using the following seven-point scale:

1.  High Public Spending, High Taxation: The party strongly advocates for high levels of public spending on public services, accompanied by high taxation to fund this expenditure. This position prioritizes extensive public services and welfare programs, emphasizing the role of the government in providing these services.
2.  Moderately High Public Spending, High Taxation: The party supports relatively high levels of public spending and is comfortable with high taxation to support this. While not as extreme as position 1, it still prioritizes significant public investment and welfare services, albeit with some consideration for tax efficiency.
3.  Moderate Public Spending, Moderate to High Taxation: The party advocates for a balanced approach with moderately high public spending and corresponding taxation. It aims to maintain robust public services but with a careful approach to avoid excessive taxation.
4.  Balanced Approach: The party supports a balanced mix of public spending and taxation. It advocates for a pragmatic approach, where public services are funded adequately without excessively high or low taxation. This position seeks to strike a middle ground between providing services and keeping taxes reasonable.
5.  Moderate Public Spending, Moderate to Low Taxation: The party favors moderately low levels of public spending and seeks to reduce taxation to a moderate extent. This position leans towards reducing the size of public services to decrease the tax burden but still maintains some level of essential public services.
6.  Moderately Low Public Spending, Low Taxation: The party supports low levels of public spending on public services and correspondingly low levels of taxation. This position emphasizes reducing the role of government in providing services and seeks to minimize the tax burden on individuals and businesses.
7.  Low Public Spending, Low Taxation: The party strongly advocates for minimal public spending on public services and very low taxation. This position prioritizes individual responsibility and the free market, with minimal government intervention in providing services.

Dimension: Social

For the following text of a party manifesto, please classify the party position in terms of liberalism or conservatism on social lifestyle issues (including abortion, gay rights, and other related matters), using the following seven-point scale:

1.  Very Liberal: The party strongly advocates for liberal social policies, including full support for abortion rights, comprehensive LGBTQ+ rights (including marriage equality, adoption rights, and anti-discrimination laws), and other progressive social issues. It emphasizes individual freedom and equality in all aspects of social life and seeks to advance and protect these rights through robust legislative measures.
2.  Liberal with Progressive Policies: The party supports liberal social policies, promoting significant rights and protections for individuals in areas such as abortion and LGBTQ+ rights. It advocates for accessible abortion services, strong anti-discrimination laws, and broad recognition of LGBTQ+ relationships and family structures. While not as radical as the most liberal position, it still prioritizes progressive changes and protections.
3.  Moderately Liberal: The party supports liberal social policies but with some moderate constraints. It advocates for legal abortion with certain regulations, supports LGBTQ+ rights including marriage equality and anti-discrimination measures, and promotes other progressive social policies. This position seeks a balance between individual freedoms and societal norms, aiming for broad but not unrestricted liberalization.
4.  Balanced Approach: The party takes a centrist position on social lifestyle issues, seeking to balance liberal and conservative views. It supports some liberal policies such as legal abortion with restrictions and basic LGBTQ+ rights while also accommodating certain conservative perspectives. This position aims to find common ground and promote social harmony.
5.  Moderately Conservative: The party favors conservative social policies with some liberal allowances. It supports more restrictive abortion laws, such as limiting access to later-term abortions, and may support certain LGBTQ+ rights but oppose others like adoption or marriage equality. This position emphasizes traditional values while allowing for limited individual freedoms.
6.  Conservative with Traditional Values: The party strongly supports conservative social policies, advocating for significant restrictions on abortion (possibly aiming to make it illegal or highly restricted) and opposing many LGBTQ+ rights such as marriage equality and adoption. It promotes traditional family structures and social norms, emphasizing the preservation of established societal values.
7.  Very Conservative: The party strongly advocates for highly conservative social policies, including making abortion illegal in most or all cases, opposing LGBTQ+ rights (including marriage, adoption, and anti-discrimination protections), and promoting traditional, often religiously-informed, social values. This position prioritizes preserving traditional societal norms and minimizing changes to established social structures.
```

title: chat_openai() generates HTTP 400 Bad Request with IONOS API due to invalid JSON format in messages.content field
description:
### Description:
When using`chat_openai()` (tested with ellmer v0.2.1.9000) with `base_url `and `api_headers` configured for the IONOS OpenAI-compatible API, the API returns a `400 Bad Request` error:

> JSON format issue: expected string at field messages.content got instead array

Even though the input prompt is a simple string, `ellmer` internally generates JSON where `messages.content` is serialized as an array instead of a string. The IONOS API, unlike the official OpenAI API, does not accept arrays in the `content` field.

### Minimal reproducible example 
_(assuming you have an IONOS account and API key)_
```r
library(ellmer)

ionos_token <- Sys.getenv("IONOS_API_TOKEN")
ionos_url <- "https://openai.inference.de-txl.ionos.com/v1"

chat <- chat_openai(
  model = "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
  base_url = ionos_url,
  api_headers = c(Authorization = paste("Bearer", ionos_token))
)

chat$chat("hi")
# Results in error:
# Error in `req_perform_connection()`:
# ! HTTP 400 Bad Request.
# ℹ JSON format issue: expected string at field messages.content got instead array
``` 

### Expected behavior:
`ellmer` should produce JSON where the `messages.content ` field is always a string, never an array, for simple string prompts.

### Workaround
Using a direct request with `httr2 `works correctly:
``` r
library(httr2)

messages <- list(
  list(role = "system", content = "You are a helpful assistant."),
  list(role = "user", content = "hi")
)

resp <- request(file.path(ionos_url, "chat/completions")) |>
  req_headers(
    Authorization = paste("Bearer", ionos_token),
    `Content-Type` = "application/json"
  ) |>
  req_body_json(list(
    model = "meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
    messages = messages
  )) |>
  req_perform()

result <- resp_body_json(resp)
cat(result$choices[[1]]$message$content)
# How can I assist you today?
```
### Suggested fix:
`chat_openai()` should:

- Ensure internally that messages.content is always a single string and not an array,
- Or provide an option to accept preformatted message lists with strict string content,
- Possibly revise or improve the format_messages parameter for flexibility.

### Background:
IONOS is one of Germany’s largest cloud service providers and web hosting companies. They offer an OpenAI-compatible large language model API tailored for the German and European market, emphasizing data privacy and compliance with local regulations such as GDPR. 
Note: The IONOS API is advertised as OpenAI-compatible but currently rejects JSON payloads where messages.content is an array instead of a string. This differs from the official OpenAI API, which accepts both formats. It is unclear whether this difference is intentional or an implementation detail on IONOS’s side. Supporting IONOS’s API in `ellmer `would make the package much more useful for European users and companies looking for privacy-conscious AI solutions compliant with EU law. 

**Thanks for this great package!**
Looking forward to feedback and support.

title: Alternative functional interface
description:
The very wonderful package [openxlsx2](https://janmarvin.github.io/openxlsx2/) has the same sort of object oriented design as `ellmer`, but it also provides a functional interface that feels much more natural for R.

So in `xlsx2` you can use the object oriented approach:

```r
wb_workbook( # create a workbook object 
  )$add_worksheet("Motor Trend Car Road Tests" # add a worksheet
  )$add_data_table(x = mtcars # add some data
  )$open() # open it in excel
```

Or equivalently:

```r
wb_workbook() |>
  wb_add_worksheet("Motor Trend Car Road Tests") |>
  wb_add_data_table(x = mtcars) |>
  wb_open()
```

Although the two approaches do the same thing, the second feels much more natural. It also allows much more easy discovery of available functions and accessing of the help files for those functions.

Would you consider creating a similar alternative functional interface for `ellmer`? It could be a simple wrapper around the object oriented approach.

```r
chat <- function(chat_obj, ...){
  chat_obj$chat(...)
  return(chat_obj)
}
```

```r
new_chat <- chat_anthropic()
new_chat <- chat(new_chat, "what's 2 + 2")
```

HTTP 403 error running`models_aws_bedrock()` using environment variables for authentication
description:
I have been able to successfully utilize `{ellmer}` using AWS Bedrock in my team's AWS account at the day job with `chat_aws_bedrock()`, which is a **massive win** considering most of the technical hurdles I have to overcome for these resources. To pull it off, I had to do a little customization. Our IT policies discourage the use of static API credentials for AWS services, so we have to obtain "temporary" access key ID, secret access key, and session token through another means. I have been able to obtain these "just in time" versions of the credentials thanks to linking an IAM role with a Microsoft Entra ID application. I can't share the exact details, but I can show the overall process and how it relates to the issue. First, here's the workflow I use to authenticate and set up a new chat object with `ellmer::chat_aws_bedrock()`:

```r
source("auth.R")

library(paws)
library(ellmer)

my_auth_creds <- get_creds()

# using ellmer
new_chat <- withr::with_envvar(
  new = c(
    "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" = my_auth_creds$access_key_id,
    "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" = my_auth_creds$secret_access_key,
    "AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" = my_auth_creds$session_token,
    "AWS_REGION" = "us-east-1"
  ),
  chat_aws_bedrock()
)

new_chat$chat("Tell me jokes about microsoft Windows")
```

The above approach works, since `{paws.common}` will search for environment variables related to the AWS authentication in the absence of a profile supplied. However, this same approach fails with a 403 unauthorized error if I simply try using `ellmber::models_aws_bedrock()` instead:

```r
withr::with_envvar(
  new = c(
    "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID" = my_auth_creds$access_key_id,
    "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY" = my_auth_creds$secret_access_key,
    "AWS_SESSION_TOKEN" = my_auth_creds$session_token,
    "AWS_REGION" = "us-east-1"
  ),
  models_aws_bedrock()
)
```

I'm trying to figure out if this is due to the IAM role used in this workflow not having the right permissions, or if it is something that `models_aws_bedrock()` is not picking up. Happy to provide more diagnostics but it won't be able to give a 100% reprex due the confidentiality of that authentication trick to get the temp session credentials.

title: don't error for undocumented tool arguments that have defaults
description:
Suppose I have some function:

``` r
library(ellmer)

boop <- function(x, a = 1) {
  x + a
}
```

If I don't supply type definitions for the `a` argument, I now get an error from `ellmer::tool()` with the dev version of the package:

```r
tool(
  boop,
  "Boops a number by a fixed value.",
  arguments = list(x = type_number("A number to boop."))
)
#> Error in `tool()`:
#> ! Names of `arguments` must match formals of `fun`
#> • Missing type definitions: "a"
```

<sup>Created on 2025-07-16 with [reprex v2.1.1](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

From here:

https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/blob/65f19906627d4ac9da596e662ef2d424dd7912ad/R/tools-def.R#L221-L223

This feels overly strict to me; we have a few situations in btw where some arguments are purposefully not made visible to the model, but instead have defaults that we always want to be left as-is when used by a model (e.g. `env = global_env()`). Could we filter out arguments that have default values in this setdiff call to allow for arguments with defaults to not be surfaced to the model?

https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/blob/65f19906627d4ac9da596e662ef2d424dd7912ad/R/tools-def.R#L213

It's of course possible to wrap the LLM-friendly version of the tool function to not take those arguments, but this seems cumbersome.

title: preserve conversation history after interrupt
description:
Currently, if you interrupt streaming in the model of an assistant turn, nothing of what was received up to that point is preserved in the chat history:

```r
library(ellmer)

ch <- chat_anthropic(model = "claude-sonnet-4-20250514")

ch$chat("Some lorem ipsum, please.")
# Interrupt after a few tokens

ch
#> <Chat Anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-20250514 turns=0 tokens=0/0 $0.00>
```

I would expect that, instead, all of the tokens that had been streamed thus far would be present in an assistant turn, perhaps ending with a `... [Streaming interrupted.]`. If the chat was interrupted during a tool call (related to #459), a tool response like the following might be automatically appended:

```r
ellmer::ContentToolResult(
  error = "The tool call was interrupted during execution.",
  request = tool_request
)
```

My motivation here is that, in a chat app I'm working on, the reason I often want to interrupt is because the assistant is just doing too much; I'm generally fine with what's happened so far in the turn, but I want to stop and provide some direction. In that case, I don't want the model to "forget" what had happened up to that point in the turn. (Related to https://github.com/posit-dev/shinychat/issues/73.)

title: A chat produced by a function enclosed  by a namespace doesn't print tool calls
description:
Long name for a weird issue but easy to see with an example: 

```r
make_chat <- function() {
  get_current_time <- function(tz = "UTC") {
    format(Sys.time(), tz = tz, usetz = TRUE)
  }
  chat <- ellmer::chat_openai()
  chat$register_tool(ellmer::tool(
    get_current_time,
    "Gets the current time in the given time zone.",
    tz = ellmer::type_string(
      "The time zone to get the current time in. Defaults to 'UTC'.",
      required = FALSE
    )
  ))
  chat
}

chat <- make_chat()
#> Using model = "gpt-4.1".
chat$chat("what time is it?")
#> ◯ [tool call] get_current_time(tz = NULL)
#> ● #> 2025-07-10 16:45:05 UTC
#> The current time is 16:45 (4:45 PM) UTC. If you need the time in a specific 
#> time zone, let me know!


environment(make_chat) <- asNamespace("stats")
chat <- make_chat()
#> Using model = "gpt-4.1".
chat$chat("what time is it?")
#> [1] "The current time is 16:45 (4:45 PM) UTC. If you need the local time for a specific location, let me know!"
```

To work as expected the chat definition must be created somewhere else, this will work: 

``` r
make_chat2 <- function() {
  get_current_time <- function(tz = "UTC") {
    format(Sys.time(), tz = tz, usetz = TRUE)
  }
  
  # possible args and `...` can be fed to `list()` to be evaled here
  chat <- do.call(ellmer::chat_openai, list(), envir = parent.frame())
  
  chat$register_tool(ellmer::tool(
    get_current_time,
    "Gets the current time in the given time zone.",
    tz = ellmer::type_string(
      "The time zone to get the current time in. Defaults to 'UTC'.",
      required = FALSE
    )
  ))
  chat
}

environment(make_chat2) <- asNamespace("stats")
chat <- make_chat2()
#> Using model = "gpt-4.1".
chat$chat("what time is it?")
#> ◯ [tool call] get_current_time(tz = NULL)
#> ● #> 2025-07-10 17:43:31 UTC
#> The current time is 17:43 (5:43 PM) UTC. If you need the time in a specific 
#> location, let me know!
```

title: Add error handling to `parallel_chat`
description:
Thanks for this package, it's been great! 

I'm using the Azure OpenAI service with `parallel_chat` as the batch processing isn't currently available. However for some inexplicable reason, the batch of prompts I send contain some records that trigger a 4xxx response due to the content filtering policy of [Azure OpenAI](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/openai/concepts/content-filter). 

I'd like to suggest adding error handling in `parallel_chat` so the whole process doesn't fail if some errors are returned. `parallel_chat` is calling `httr2::req_perform_parallel` internally which has an `on_error` param for error handling. The easiest solution is probably just adding `...` to the function that get passed to `httr2::req_perform_parallel`, then all params will be available in `parallel_chat`. 

I've made the update in `parallel_chat` and `parallel_chat_structured` and happy to open up a PR, but currently don't have permission.

title: pass fixed args to tool invoked functions
description:
Say I'd like to build parameterized a tool around `browseURL()`, and use the `browser` argument to refine the behavior, but not allow the llm to change it, I'd like this to work:

```
tool_browse_url <- function(browser) {
  tool(
    browseURL,
    "Browse to the given URL",
    url = type_string("A valid URL")
    browser = browser # <----   not a llm parameter because not a "ellmer::Type" object
  )
}
chat$register_tool(tool_browse_url(my_browser))
```

Or

```
tool_browse_url <- function(browser) {
  tool(
    browseURL,
    "Browse to the given URL",
    url = type_string("A valid URL"),
    .fixed_args = list(browser = browser) # <----   a new .fixed_args argument
  )
}
chat$register_tool(tool_browse_url(my_browser))
```

An alternative is to use options to set global behavior (in fact already implemented in `browseURL()`) but it's not very satisfying as it is global, and it forbids us to build agents around the same functions but with different fixed args, e.g. a safari agent and a chrome agent in the same session.

The best way I found is to do something like : 

```
tool_browse_url <- function(browser) {
  browseURL <- function(url) utils::browseURL(url, browser)
  tool(
    browseURL,
    "Browse to the given URL",
    url = type_string("A valid URL")
  )
}
chat$register_tool(tool_browse_url(my_browser))
```

But then when turns are printed we will miss the `browser` argument.

Is there a way to do this or would you be able to make it possible?

title: Could tools() accept namespaced functions ?
description:
Printing the invoked function call is very helpful, but if we call packaged functions it's not as reproducible as it could be, could we extend the restriction to symbols to allow at least calls to `::`, and maybe `:::`, `@` and `$`.

``` r
library(ellmer)

# works
chat1 <- ellmer::chat_openai()
#> Using model = "gpt-4.1".
chat1$register_tool(tool(paste0, "concat 2 strings", x = type_string(), y = type_string()))
chat1$chat("concat 'a' and 'b'")
#> ◯ [tool call] paste0(x = "a", y = "b")

chat2 <- ellmer::chat_openai()
```

title: Could we have tools return images too ?
description:
The tool doc says : 

> The output of the tool call will be interpreted by the LLM, just as if you had typed that information into the data. That means you’ll generally want to produce text or other atomic vectors. For more complex data, ellmer will automatically serialize the result to JSON, which LLMs generally seem to be good at understanding.

As I understand it is not possible to provide images to llm through tools with ellmer at the moment.
For iterating on image generation, or using a screen capture tool to guide a tool we need to be able to have our functions output images.

Some models might take in sound or video or soon will too, some might accept, xlsx or pdf, so it might make sense for `tool()` to have a `content_type` arg defaulting to "text" and that can be flexibly extended, and the tool functions would be expected to return a path.

title: models_ollama() strips subpaths from base_url
description:
Our company has an Ollama server running behind a reverse proxy on a subpath URL; https://example.com/ollama. When running `ellmer::chat_ollama(base_url = "https://example.com/ollama", model = "gemma3:4b")`, I get the error:

```Error in `resp_body_json()`:
! Unexpected content type "text/html".
• Expecting type "application/json" or suffix "json".
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.```

Since version 0.2.0, ellmer::chat_ollama() [always runs ellmer::models_ollama()](https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/blob/87f442443471e87386799c59db90f9fbd3c7bd43/R/provider-ollama.R#L52) to check that the model is available before running. However, that function strips away the end of the base_url with req_url_path() so what should be https://example.com/ollama/api/tags results in https://example.com/api/tags

I think the issue will be resolved if references to req_url_path() are changed to req_url_path_append() in [provider-ollama.R](https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/blob/87f442443471e87386799c59db90f9fbd3c7bd43/R/provider-ollama.R#L117), which is consistent with the other models_*() functions in the package.

I will try to fix the issue by setting `options(ellmer_timeout_s = ???)` to a higher number than 5 minutes (https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/issues/553#issuecomment-2936329085), but I am still wondering what the underlying issue actually is causing this error. library(ellmer)

```r
library(processx)

  is_connected <- test_connection(logical = TRUE)
  if (is_connected) {
    return(invisible(TRUE))
  }
  rlang::abort('`ollama` is not running.')
}

insistent_ollama_is_ready <- insistently(

p$kill()
```

description:

This model provider and model is also included in my .Rprofile file as `options(.gander_chat = ellmer::chat_ollama(model = "devstral:latest"))`.

I knew the model was present, because i pulled it directly with ollama and it shows up with `ollama list` as:

title: [question] how to restart errored parallel_chat_structured?
description:
I just successfully ran 15k queries in less than 2 minutes using parallel_chat_structured, which is amazing 😲 (especially for cheap models like gpt-4.1-nano).

Given that, my question is: if one or more queries return an errored response (e.g., the famous "timeout"), is there a way to restart the query only on the not-yet-succesfully submitted prompts, without losing the successfully submitted ones?

My first idea is to use `purrr::safely`:

```
...
safe_pcs <- purrr::safely(ellmer::parallel_chat_structured)
res <- safe_pcs(chat, prompts, type, convert = FALSE)
```

Would this be the suggested way to go, or would you suggest another way?

Thank you!

title: SSL/TLS connection timeout
`chat_databricks()` support for structured outputs is broken
description:
Pulling the example from the unit tests:

```r
article_summary <- type_object(
  "Summary of the article. Preserve existing case.",
  title = type_string("Content title"),
  author = type_string("Name of the author")
)
prompt <- "
    # Apples are tasty
    By Hadley Wickham

    Apples are delicious and tasty and I like to eat them.
    Except for red delicious, that is. They are NOT delicious.
"
chat <- chat_databricks()
chat$chat_structured(prompt, type = article_summary)
```

Yields:

```
Error in `req_perform()`:
! HTTP 400 Bad Request.
• {"message":"response_format: Extra inputs are not permitted"}
```

After some debugging and looking at their [structured outputs example](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/model-serving/structured-outputs#use-structured-outputs), I think that the wrapping we are doing here might be at issue: https://github.com/tidyverse/ellmer/blob/9b09eba609d76702d4d4dab1079228f925a64547/R/chat.R#L236-L237

This wrapping ought not to apply to `ProviderDatabricks`. It's not straightforward to opt out of it, though, because we do otherwise need to inherit from `ProviderOpenAI`.

title: `chat_databricks()` barfs when tool calls are registered
description:
It seems that Databricks's tool serialization is not OpenAI compatible after all:

```r
> chat <- chat_databricks(model = "databricks-claude-3-7-sonnet")
> chat$register_tool(tool(
  function() format(Sys.Date()),
  .name = "current_date",
  .description = "Returns the current date in ISO 8601 format."
))
> chat$chat("What's the current date in Y-M-D format?")
Error in `req_perform_connection()` at elmer/R/httr2.R:37:5:
! HTTP 400 Bad Request.
• tools.0.custom.strict: Extra inputs are not permitted
```

Reported by @blairj09.

title: Request to add headers to chat_openai()
description:
My organization requires that I access OpenAI via a proxy. It's easy enough change the URL in the `chat_openai()` function using the `base_url` argument and the API key using the `api_key` argument. However, my organization's proxy also requires the specification of an organization key. Below is the code that I use to make requests using `httr2`:

```
gpt_body <- list(
    messages = messages_list,
    model = gpt_model,
    temperature = resp_temp,
    max_tokens = max_tokens
  )

  gpt_response <- request("https://llm-proxy.sandbox.indeed.net/openai/v1") |>
    req_url_path_append("chat/completions") |>
    req_auth_bearer_token(indeed_api_key) |>
    req_headers(
      "OpenAI-Organization" = indeed_org_key,
      "x-indeed-redact-allow" = "LOCATION,PERSON"
    ) |>
    req_body_json(gpt_body) |>
    req_retry(max_tries = 5) |>
    req_perform()
```

The list in `gpt_body` contains the prompt and request params. `gpt_response` would contain the response from OpneAI upon making a request that includes request headers. My suggestion would be to include req_headers in the creation of the `base_request` method of the ProviderOpenAI class if possible:

```
method(base_request, ProviderOpenAI) <- function(provider) {
  req <- request(provider@base_url)
  req <- req_auth_bearer_token(req, provider@api_key)
  **req <- req_headers (req, openai_headers)**
  req <- req_retry(req, max_tries = 2)
  req <- ellmer_req_timeout(req, stream)
  req <- ellmer_req_user_agent(req)
  req <- base_request_error(provider, req)
  req
}
```

I'm not sure if this would be useful to others.

title: Error in provider@model: No applicable method for @ applied to class “ellmer::ProviderDeepSeek”
description:
Hello everyone,

I'm looking for some help and guidance.

I'm building an AI assistant using the ellmer and shinychat packages with a DeepSeek API hosted on a private server. Here is a simplified version of my code:

`Sys.setenv(DEEPSEEK_API_KEY = "empty")`

```R
ui <- bslib::page_fluid(
  chat_ui("chat")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  chat <- ellmer::chat_deepseek(
    system_prompt = '',
    base_url = 'my-host-API address',
    api_key = 'empty',
    model = "deepseek-r1"
  )
 
  observeEvent(input$chat_user_input, {
    stream <- chat$stream_async(input$chat_user_input)
    chat_append("chat", stream)
  })
}
shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Everything works fine until the end of the thinking process, where I encounter the following error:

```
> Error in provider@model : 
>   no applicable method for '@' applied to an object of class "ellmer::ProviderDeepSeek"
```

In the R console, it also shows:

```
> 错误于provider@model:  没有适用于`@`的方法应用于类“ellmer::ProviderDeepSeek”的对象
收捲时出错: 已经在评估：递归缺省参数参考还是早先原来的问题？
Error: no more error handlers available (recursive errors?); invoking 'abort' restart
```

It seems like it's trying to access an S4 slot using @, but the object might be an R6 or a list instead.

Does anyone know how to resolve this issue? Is this a bug, or am I misusing the ellmer::chat_deepseek function?

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Best regards,

title: Using future_promise and stream_async together in Shiny Extended task
More control over output with structured data prompts
description:
It would be nice to have the option to receive outputs back from structured data prompts as JSON strings so that the user can parse it as they would like (or not parse at all). I presumed that this is what I would get when specifying `convert = FALSE` but I misread the docs. I haven't dug too deep but I presume responses always get parsed with `httr2::resp_body_json()` so this might be less than trivial to allow for.

The reason for this request is that if the response from the structured data prompt is to be used somewhere outside of R, the JSON parsing could lose fidelity to the underlying JSON schema when serialized again.

Somewhat related to #527.

title: Allow JSON string to structured chat `type`
description:
I work in an organization where non-R developers have defined JSON schemas that we want to use to prescribe the output from structured chats in some pipelines we are building with ellmer.

These schemas can be pretty complex and also change over time and it would be quite cumbersome to continually manually translate these schemas to the `type_*()` definitions in R (which then in turn get translated back to JSON anyway).

To address this use case, could ellmer allow a JSON string type as an argument to `type` in `$structured_chat()`? If this seems acceptable I'd be happy to work on a PR.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with ellmer
description:
I am putting this here, because it took me a lot of searching, google-ing and then [rseeking](https://rseek.org/) to find this. I think it should be added to the ellmer docs somewhere.

To use [RAG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retrieval-augmented_generation) in R there seem to be two options:
- [ragnar](https://github.com/tidyverse/ragnar) which works with ellmer
- [RAGFlowChainR](https://github.com/knowusuboaky/RAGFlowChainR) which works with [chatLLM](https://github.com/knowusuboaky/chatLLM)

title: Support local .databrickscfg for Databricks
description:
[Databricks client unified authentication](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/unified-auth) is an established way for managing Databricks authentication that includes support for [Databricks configuration profiles](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/auth/config-profiles). Ellmer should support profiles defined in these config files. Currently, if I authenticate using the Databricks CLI (`databricks auth login`) and name the resulting profile `DEFAULT`, I get a `~/.databrickscfg` file that contains:
```
[DEFAULT]
host      = <DATABRICKS-HOST>
auth_type = databricks-cli
```

This profile can be correctly used by other tools that rely on Databricks client unified authentication (like the [Databricks Python SDK](https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/sdk-python)). However, `ellmer` doesn't currently pick up on this file or the profiles defined and instead falls back on interactive browser authentication:

```
> chat <- ellmer::chat_databricks(model = "databricks-claude-3-7-sonnet")
Error in `databricks_workspace()`:
! Can't find env var `DATABRICKS_HOST`.
Show Traceback
```

This is a difference compared to `chatlas`, which "just works" with the defined `DEFAULT` profile:
```
>>> import chatlas
... chat = chatlas.ChatDatabricks(model = "databricks-claude-3-7-sonnet")
... chat.chat("Who are you?")
[05/21/25 09:51:13] INFO     chatlas - Provider 'Databricks' generated a response of 101 tokens  [_tokens.py](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-sandbox/workbench/workbench.html#):[30](vscode-file://vscode-app/Applications/Positron.app/Contents/Resources/app/out/vs/code/electron-sandbox/workbench/workbench.html#)
                             from an input of 11 tokens.                                                      
                                                                                                              
I'm Claude, an AI assistant created by Anthropic to be helpful, harmless, and honest. I can have              
conversations, answer questions, assist with various tasks like writing and analysis, and generate different  
kinds of content. I aim to be thoughtful, ethical, and provide balanced perspectives. I have certain          
limitations - I don't have the ability to access the internet, run code, or interact with other systems unless
specifically enabled to do so. How can I help you today?
```

title: Fix Example 5: `.additional_properties = TRUE` requires `convert = FALSE`
description:
I noticed a minor issue with Example 5 in the vignette `structured-data.Rmd`

```r

type_characteristics <- type_object(
  "All characteristics",
  .additional_properties = TRUE
)

prompt <- "
  Given a description of a character, your task is to extract all the characteristics of that character.

  <description>
  The man is tall, with a beard and a scar on his left cheek. He has a deep voice and wears a black leather jacket.
  </description>
"

chat <- chat_anthropic()
str(chat$chat_structured(prompt, type = type_characteristics))

```

Although `chat_anthropic()` was used, this returns an empty list (`list()`), even though you would expect to receive a result. The issue is that 'Working with unknown keys' only works if you set `convert = FALSE`. The same is true if you use unknown keys in a tool, for example:

```r

chat$register_tool(
      tool(
        update_characteristics,
        "Updates the characteristics list",
        characteristics_list =
          type_object(
            "All characteristics",
            .additional_properties = TRUE
          ),
        .convert = FALSE # Necessary, otherwise it will always return list()
      )
    )

```

So I think for Example 5, `convert` should be set to `FALSE` and maybe a small hint that this is necessary (also for tools) would be also useful!

title: Tool calls are printed without argument conversion
description:
Small formatting issue that we should try to run tool arguments through `tool_request_args()` so they reflect the converted data structures before echoing the tool request.

``` r
pkgload::load_all()
#> ℹ Loading ellmer

tool <- tool(
  function(greeting = c("Hello", "Goodbye"), name = "your") {
    args <<- list(greeting = greeting, name = name)
    cli::format_inline("{greeting}, {.and {name}}!")
  },
  .description = "Random number between 1 and 10.",
  .name = "greet",
  greeting = type_array(
    description = "Choose a greeting",
    items = type_enum(values = c("Hello", "Goodbye")),
  ),
  name = type_array("Name or names to greet", items = type_string())
)

req <- ContentToolRequest(
  id = "test",
  name = "greet",
  arguments = list(
    greeting = list("Hello"),
    name = list("Hadley", "Simon")
  ),
  tool = tool
)
```
``` r
cat(format(req))
#> [tool request (test)]: greet(greeting = list("Hello"), name = list("Hadley", "Simon"))
# Should be...
#> [tool request (test)]: greet(greeting = "Hello", name = c("Hadley", "Simon"))
str(tool_request_args(req))
#> List of 2
#>  $ greeting: Factor w/ 2 levels "Hello","Goodbye": 1
#>  $ name    : chr [1:2] "Hadley" "Simon"
```
